axiam_sdk

Official Python client SDK for AXIAM (Access eXtended Identity and Authorization Management).

Re-exports the public surface: the sync AxiamClient and async AsyncAxiamClient REST entry points, the AuthError/AuthzError/ NetworkError exception taxonomy (CONTRACT.md §2), and the request/response models (LoginResult, User, AccessCheck, AccessResult, BatchCheckResult, UserInfo). See CONTRACT.md §1-§10 for the cross-language behavioral contract this SDK conforms to.

This module MUST remain importable with ONLY the runtime dependencies declared in [project.dependencies] (httpx, grpcio, aio-pika, pydantic, PyJWT) — the optional web-framework integrations (axiam_sdk.fastapi, axiam_sdk.django, see [project.optional-dependencies]) MUST NOT be imported from here.

  9cross-language behavioral contract this SDK conforms to.

class DecisionMemo: 
 78class DecisionMemo:
 79    """A bounded, TTL-clamped decision memo.
 80
 81    ``ttl_ms == 0`` means **disabled** — not "cache for zero milliseconds".
 82    That is the default, and both :meth:`get` and :meth:`set` become no-ops.
 83
 84    Thread-safe: the sync client is commonly shared across a thread pool, and a
 85    cache that corrupted under concurrency would be a worse bug than the one it
 86    is optimising away.
 87    """
 88
 89    __slots__ = ("_ttl_ms", "_entries", "_now", "_lock")
 90
 91    def __init__(self, ttl_ms: float = 0.0, now: Callable[[], float] | None = None) -> None:
 92        """
 93        :param ttl_ms: requested TTL in milliseconds; ``0`` disables the memo and
 94            any value above :data:`MAX_TTL_MS` is clamped to it.
 95        :param now: injected monotonic clock in seconds, so the TTL can be
 96            tested without waiting.
 97        """
 98        self._ttl_ms = min(max(float(ttl_ms), 0.0), MAX_TTL_MS)
 99        self._entries: OrderedDict[str, tuple[object, float]] = OrderedDict()
100        self._now = now if now is not None else time.monotonic
101        self._lock = threading.Lock()
102
103    @property
104    def enabled(self) -> bool:
105        """Whether this memo does anything. ``False`` for the default config."""
106        return self._ttl_ms > 0
107
108    @property
109    def effective_ttl_ms(self) -> float:
110        """The TTL after clamping."""
111        return self._ttl_ms
112
113    def get(self, key: str) -> object | None:
114        """A live decision for *key*, if one is memoized and unexpired."""
115        if not self.enabled:
116            return None
117        with self._lock:
118            entry = self._entries.get(key)
119            if entry is None:
120                return None
121            decision, stored_at = entry
122            if (self._now() - stored_at) * 1000.0 >= self._ttl_ms:
123                del self._entries[key]
124                return None
125            # Returned whole, including ``reason_code``: §17.1 rule 5 forbids
126            # returning ``allowed`` while dropping the code, which would make
127            # the field intermittently absent — worse than never having had it.
128            return decision
129
130    def set(self, key: str, decision: object) -> None:
131        """Memoize a decision the server actually returned.
132
133        Callers must only reach here on success. §17.1 rule 7 forbids
134        negative-caching a failure: memoizing a transport error as a deny would
135        turn a blip into a TTL-long outage, and memoizing it as an allow is
136        unthinkable.
137        """
138        if not self.enabled:
139            return
140        with self._lock:
141            self._entries.pop(key, None)
142            self._entries[key] = (decision, self._now())
143            while len(self._entries) > _MAX_ENTRIES:
144                self._entries.popitem(last=False)
145
146    def clear(self) -> None:
147        """Drop every entry (§17.1 rule 9).
148
149        Called on login, verify_mfa, refresh and logout. Entries are keyed by
150        subject, not by session, so a re-authentication as a *different*
151        principal would otherwise read the previous principal's decisions.
152        """
153        with self._lock:
154            self._entries.clear()
155
156    def report_clamp(self, requested_ms: float, telemetry: TelemetryDispatcher) -> None:
157        """Emit a :class:`ConfigClamped` if the requested TTL was clamped (§19.2 rule 6).
158
159        This is the clamp that matters most to get right: an operator who set a
160        60-second TTL believes their staleness bound is 60 seconds. It is five,
161        and without this event nothing anywhere says so.
162
163        Nothing is emitted when the requested value was already inside the
164        limit, or when the memo is disabled — an event that fires when nothing
165        happened trains its reader to ignore it.
166        """
167        if not telemetry.installed or requested_ms <= 0.0 or requested_ms == self._ttl_ms:
168            return
169        telemetry.emit(
170            ConfigClamped(
171                setting="decision_memo_ttl_ms",
172                requested=str(requested_ms),
173                effective=str(self._ttl_ms),
174                contract_reference="§17.1 rule 2",
175            )
176        )
177
178    def __len__(self) -> int:
179        """Number of live entries, for tests."""
180        with self._lock:
181            return len(self._entries)

A bounded, TTL-clamped decision memo.

ttl_ms == 0 means disabled — not "cache for zero milliseconds". That is the default, and both get() and set() become no-ops.

Thread-safe: the sync client is commonly shared across a thread pool, and a cache that corrupted under concurrency would be a worse bug than the one it is optimising away.

__version__ = '1.0.0b04'
class AxiamClient(axiam_sdk._client._AxiamClientBase, axiam_sdk.management.ops.ManagementNamespaces): 
 660class AxiamClient(_AxiamClientBase, ManagementNamespaces):
 661    """The AXIAM SDK's sync REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10).
 662
 663    ``client.login(...)`` returns a typed :class:`~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult`
 664    with ``mfa_required`` (SC#1). For the async twin, use
 665    :class:`~axiam_sdk.AsyncAxiamClient` (SDK-Q08) — a separate class, not an
 666    ``async_*`` method on this one.
 667    """
 668
 669    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 670    # Lifecycle (D-19)
 671    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 672
 673    def __enter__(self) -> AxiamClient:
 674        """Context-manager entry — returns ``self`` (D-19); no separate
 675        setup beyond what ``__init__`` already did."""
 676        return self
 677
 678    def __exit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
 679        """Context-manager exit — always calls :meth:`close`, regardless of
 680        whether the ``with`` block raised (D-19)."""
 681        self.close()
 682
 683    def close(self) -> None:
 684        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
 685
 686        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
 687        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
 688
 689        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
 690        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
 691        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
 692        restart and resume; a ``close()`` that logged out would silently end
 693        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
 694        ending the session is what you want.
 695
 696        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
 697        rather than silently reconnecting.
 698        """
 699        self._closed = True
 700        self._decision_memo.clear()
 701        self._session.close()
 702
 703    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 704    # login / verify_mfa
 705    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 706
 707    def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 708        """``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (CONTRACT.md §1). Returns a typed
 709        :class:`LoginResult`; check ``mfa_required`` before assuming the
 710        session is established (SC#1)."""
 711        self._ensure_open()
 712        self._on_credential_change()
 713        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 714            "POST", LOGIN_PATH, json=self._login_body(email, password)
 715        )
 716        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 717        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 718
 719    def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 720        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
 721
 722        Returns the same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
 723        ``mfa_required`` case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.
 724
 725        What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither
 726        useful without the account's registration record **and** the tenant's
 727        OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request
 728        log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password,
 729        because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database
 730        is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not
 731        offer. It does **not** protect against a compromised AXIAM server.
 732
 733        Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server
 734        proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the
 735        server during the handshake, so opening ``KE2`` *is* the proof that it
 736        holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an ``M2`` check in
 737        capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now
 738        nothing to skip.
 739
 740        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
 741            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
 742            SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not ``AuthError``: reporting a
 743            configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to
 744            reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to
 745            :meth:`login`.
 746        :raises AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist,
 747            an account with no registration record, and a server that does not
 748            hold the record — indistinguishable by design. **Nothing is sent to
 749            ``login/finish`` in that case** (§23.4 rule 7).
 750
 751        **The ``mode`` field decides what happens after a failed exchange**, and
 752        nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). ``login/start`` carries the tenant's
 753        ``opaque_mode``:
 754
 755        * ``"optional"`` — this method retries over :meth:`login` with the same
 756          credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's
 757          outcome. Under ``optional`` an account with no record is the ordinary
 758          case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an
 759          operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a
 760          password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every
 761          user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state ``optional`` exists
 762          to serve.
 763        * ``"required"``, an unrecognised value, or **no ``mode`` at all** (a
 764          server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is
 765          retried over :meth:`login`. It would be refused anyway: ``required``
 766          answers ``403 opaque_required`` for every principal in the tenant, so
 767          trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.
 768
 769        ``mode`` is **not** downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a
 770        hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer ``404`` and get
 771        the fallback whatever it puts here. ``required`` is what closes that,
 772        server-side, by refusing ``/auth/login`` before examining any
 773        credential.
 774
 775        This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by
 776        default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is
 777        the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by
 778        someone holding the OPRF seed.
 779        """
 780        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
 781
 782        self._ensure_open()
 783        self._on_credential_change()
 784
 785        exchange = start_login(password)
 786
 787        # One round trip, always. SRP had to guess a group before the server
 788        # named one and restart the exchange if it guessed wrong; ``KE1`` does
 789        # not depend on the KSF.
 790        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 791            "POST",
 792            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
 793            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
 794        )
 795        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 796        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 797            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
 798        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
 799
 800        try:
 801            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
 802        except AuthError:
 803            # §23.4 rule 7. `KE3` is not sent either way; `mode` — and only
 804            # `mode` — decides whether the plaintext path may be tried.
 805            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
 806                raise
 807            return self.login(username_or_email, password)
 808
 809        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 810            "POST",
 811            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
 812            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
 813        )
 814        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 815        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
 816            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
 817        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 818
 819    def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 820        """Build a registration record to send with any request that sets a
 821        password (user creation, change-password, reset completion).
 822
 823        The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to
 824        arrive with the request or not at all.
 825
 826        Performs a ``register/start`` round trip, which the SRP verifier this
 827        replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's
 828        oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid
 829        record.
 830
 831        Note the absence of an ``identity`` argument. The SRP version required
 832        the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a
 833        verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential
 834        identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.
 835
 836        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
 837            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
 838            SDK cannot perform.
 839        """
 840        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
 841
 842        self._ensure_open()
 843        exchange = start_registration(password)
 844
 845        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 846            "POST",
 847            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
 848            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request),
 849        )
 850        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 851        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 852            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
 853        started = response.json()
 854
 855        return {
 856            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
 857            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
 858                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
 859            ),
 860        }
 861
 862    def verify_mfa(self, mfa_token: Any, code: str) -> LoginResult:
 863        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — completes the
 864        two-phase flow started by :meth:`login` when ``mfa_required`` was
 865        true."""
 866        self._ensure_open()
 867        self._on_credential_change()
 868        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 869            "POST", MFA_VERIFY_PATH, json=self._mfa_verify_body(mfa_token, code)
 870        )
 871        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 872        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 873
 874    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 875    # refresh
 876    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 877
 878    def refresh(self) -> None:
 879        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
 880        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
 881        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
 882        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
 883        self._ensure_open()
 884        self._on_credential_change()
 885        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
 886        if not observed_access:
 887            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
 888
 889        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
 890        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
 891        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
 892        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
 893        self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_sync(
 894            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_sync(tenant_id, org_id)
 895        )
 896
 897    def _do_refresh_sync(self, tenant_id: str, org_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 898        """Perform the actual ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` call — the
 899        ``do_refresh`` closure passed to
 900        :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.refresh_if_needed_sync`
 901        by :meth:`refresh`. Not called directly by SDK users; always routed
 902        through the single-flight guard so concurrent 401s collapse into
 903        one in-flight call (§9)."""
 904        # The literal /api/v1/auth/refresh path is required so the
 905        # Path-scoped axiam_refresh cookie attaches (Pitfall 4).
 906        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 907            "POST", "/api/v1/auth/refresh", json=self._refresh_body(tenant_id, org_id)
 908        )
 909        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 910        return self._handle_refresh_response(response)
 911
 912    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 913    # logout
 914    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 915
 916    def logout(self) -> None:
 917        """``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` (CONTRACT.md §1)."""
 918        self._ensure_open()
 919        self._on_credential_change()
 920        session_id = self._session_id_for_logout()
 921        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
 922            "POST", LOGOUT_PATH, json={"session_id": session_id}
 923        )
 924        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
 925        if response.status_code >= 300:
 926            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "logout failed", response=response)
 927        self._session.refresh_guard = type(self._session.refresh_guard)()
 928
 929    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 930    # REST authz: check_access / can / batch_check (Task 3)
 931    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 932
 933    def check_access(
 934        self,
 935        action: str,
 936        resource_id: str,
 937        scope: str | None = None,
 938        *,
 939        subject_id: str | None = None,
 940    ) -> AccessResult:
 941        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
 942
 943        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
 944        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
 945        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
 946        declarative ``require_access`` helpers (§11) pass to check the
 947        *request's* authenticated user.
 948        """
 949        self._ensure_open()
 950        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
 951        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
 952        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 953        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
 954        if memoized is not None:
 955            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
 956            return memoized
 957
 958        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 959        wire = self._authz_post_sync(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
 960        result = AccessResult(**wire)
 961
 962        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
 963        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
 964        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
 965        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
 966        return result
 967
 968    def can(self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None) -> bool:
 969        """Alias for ``check_access`` returning only the allowed boolean
 970        (CONTRACT.md §1 note, browser/UI scenarios)."""
 971        return self.check_access(action, resource_id, scope).allowed
 972
 973    def batch_check(self, checks: list[AccessCheck]) -> list[AccessResult]:
 974        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check/batch`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — results
 975        returned in the same order as ``checks``."""
 976        self._ensure_open()
 977        body = {"checks": [c.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for c in checks]}
 978        wire = self._authz_post_sync(BATCH_CHECK_PATH, body, operation="batch_check")
 979        return BatchCheckResult(**wire).results
 980
 981    def _authz_post_sync(
 982        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], *, operation: str
 983    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 984        """POST an authz request body to *path* under the §16 retry policy.
 985
 986        The call is a ``POST`` but changes no server state, so it is
 987        retry-eligible: §16.2's test is "changes no server state", NOT "is a
 988        GET". Gating on the verb would exclude the single most important
 989        operation this policy covers.
 990
 991        The §9.3 refresh-then-retry-once on a 401 is a *different* mechanism and
 992        stays inside one §16 attempt: a 401 means the token expired, which
 993        refreshing fixes, and neither backing off nor counting it against the
 994        transport-failure budget would make sense.
 995        """
 996        return retry_sync(
 997            lambda attempt: self._authz_post_sync_once(path, body, operation, attempt),
 998            operation=operation,
 999            enabled=self._retry_enabled,
1000            telemetry=self._telemetry,
1001        )
1002
1003    def _authz_post_sync_once(
1004        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], operation: str, attempt: int
1005    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
1006        """One §16 attempt, with its §19 request pair."""
1007        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1008        with self._telemetry.request(operation, "POST", path, attempt) as span:
1009            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1010
1011            if response.status_code == httpx.codes.UNAUTHORIZED:
1012                response = self._retry_after_refresh_sync(request)
1013
1014            span.status = response.status_code
1015            if response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code >= 300:
1016                raise error_from_http_status(
1017                    response.status_code, "authz check failed", response=response
1018                )
1019            span.outcome = "success"
1020            result: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
1021            return result
1022
1023    def _retry_after_refresh_sync(self, original_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
1024        """On a 401, refresh exactly once (via the shared single-flight
1025        guard) then retry the failed authz call exactly once. A second
1026        failure propagates through the caller's own status check (§9.3, no
1027        retry loop)."""
1028        self.refresh()
1029        retry_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1030            original_request.method,
1031            original_request.url,
1032            content=original_request.content,
1033            headers={
1034                k: v
1035                for k, v in original_request.headers.items()
1036                if k.lower() not in ("content-length", "x-csrf-token")
1037            },
1038        )
1039        return self._session._send_sync(retry_request)
1040
1041    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1042    # OIDC / SSO relying-party helpers (CONTRACT.md §12, Task T3)
1043    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1044
1045    def oidc_discover(self) -> OidcConfiguration:
1046        """``GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
1047        fetch the OIDC discovery document, cached per origin with a
1048        ≥5-minute TTL and single-flight de-duplication of concurrent calls
1049        (§12.3 rule 6)."""
1050
1051        def fetch() -> OidcConfiguration:
1052            """Perform the actual discovery-document GET; called by the
1053            discovery cache at most once per cache miss/expiry."""
1054            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("GET", DISCOVERY_PATH)
1055            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1056            return self._parse_discovery_response(response)
1057
1058        return self._discovery_cache.get_sync(self._discovery_origin_key(), fetch)
1059
1060    def oidc_begin(
1061        self,
1062        *,
1063        configuration: OidcConfiguration,
1064        redirect_uri: str,
1065        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1066        extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
1067    ) -> AuthorizationRequest:
1068        """Build an authorization request (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — **pure
1069        local computation, no network I/O**. Nothing is stored: persist
1070        the returned ``state``, ``nonce``, and ``code_verifier`` yourself
1071        (§12.3 rule 1)."""
1072        return self._oidc_begin_impl(
1073            configuration=configuration,
1074            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
1075            scope=scope,
1076            extra_params=extra_params,
1077        )
1078
1079    def oidc_par(
1080        self,
1081        *,
1082        request: AuthorizationRequest,
1083        redirect_uri: str,
1084        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1085        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1086        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1087    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
1088        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
1089        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
1090        with.
1091
1092        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
1093        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
1094        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
1095        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
1096        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
1097        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
1098
1099        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
1100        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
1101        authorize any other way (§21.1).
1102
1103        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
1104        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
1105
1106        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
1107        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
1108        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
1109        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
1110
1111        Raises:
1112            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1113                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
1114            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
1115        """
1116        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1117        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
1118        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
1119        http_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1120        response = self._session._send_sync(http_request)
1121        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)
1122
1123    def oidc_exchange(
1124        self,
1125        *,
1126        code: str,
1127        code_verifier: SecretStr | str,
1128        redirect_uri: str,
1129        nonce: str,
1130        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1131        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1132    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1133        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=authorization_code``
1134        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — exchange an authorization code for a token
1135        set, validating the returned ID token in full before returning
1136        (§12.4). On ANY §12.4 failure the whole token set is discarded and
1137        ``AuthError`` is raised with the matching reason code (§12.4
1138        rule 7) — the access/refresh token from the same response is never
1139        returned."""
1140        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1141        form = self._exchange_form(
1142            code=code, code_verifier=code_verifier, redirect_uri=redirect_uri
1143        )
1144        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1145        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1146        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1147        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, nonce)
1148
1149    def oidc_refresh(
1150        self,
1151        *,
1152        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
1153        scope: str | None = None,
1154        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1155        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1156    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1157        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
1158        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
1159
1160        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
1161        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
1162        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
1163        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
1164        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
1165        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
1166        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
1167        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
1168        interleave.
1169        """
1170
1171        def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
1172            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
1173            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_sync`
1174            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
1175            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
1176            config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1177            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
1178            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1179            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1180            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1181            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
1182            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1183
1184        def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
1185            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
1186            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
1187            :meth:`refresh` call."""
1188            token_set: OidcTokenSet = self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_sync(do_refresh)
1189            return token_set
1190
1191        result: OidcTokenSet = self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_sync.run(under_guard)
1192        return result
1193
1194    def login_client_credentials(
1195        self,
1196        *,
1197        scope: str | None = None,
1198        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1199        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1200    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1201        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=client_credentials``
1202        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — service-account machine-to-machine login.
1203        Requests no ``openid`` scope, so the response carries no
1204        ``id_token``.
1205
1206        Raises:
1207            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — this
1208                grant cannot be performed by a public client.
1209        """
1210        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1211        form = self._client_credentials_form(scope=scope)
1212        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1213        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1214        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1215        # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to this grant.
1216        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1217
1218    def device_authorize(
1219        self,
1220        *,
1221        scope: str | None = None,
1222        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1223        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1224    ) -> DeviceAuthorization:
1225        """``POST /oauth2/device_authorization`` (CONTRACT.md §14.1) — start
1226        the device grant and obtain the code pair.
1227
1228        **Unauthenticated by design.** A device that cannot show a browser
1229        also cannot hold a client secret, so this never sends
1230        ``client_secret`` and never refuses a client built without one.
1231
1232        Raises:
1233            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1234                ``device_authorization_endpoint``.
1235        """
1236        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1237        form = self._device_authorize_form(scope=scope)
1238        url = self._device_authorization_url(config, tenant_id)
1239        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1240        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1241        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
1242            raise error_from_oauth2_response(
1243                response.status_code, response, "device authorization request failed"
1244            )
1245        return self._build_device_authorization(response.json())
1246
1247    def device_poll(
1248        self,
1249        *,
1250        device_code: SecretStr | str,
1251        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1252        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1253    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1254        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the device-code grant (§14.1) — **one**
1255        poll attempt.
1256
1257        The raw single call, so an application driving its own loop (a UI
1258        rendering a countdown, say) can. The five RFC 8628 §3.5 answers
1259        surface as ``OAuthProtocolError`` — ``authorization_pending`` and
1260        ``slow_down`` included — so a hand-rolled loop sees exactly what
1261        :meth:`device_login` sees. Most callers want :meth:`device_login`.
1262        """
1263        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1264        form = self._device_poll_form(device_code=device_code)
1265        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1266        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1267        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1268        # No nonce: the device grant has no authorization request to carry one.
1269        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1270
1271    def device_login(
1272        self,
1273        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None],
1274        *,
1275        scope: str | None = None,
1276        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1277        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1278    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1279        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
1280        user code, poll to completion.
1281
1282        ``on_user_code`` is called with the :class:`DeviceAuthorization`
1283        **before the first poll** — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have
1284        had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK
1285        never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink
1286        panel) is the application's decision.
1287
1288        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
1289        set rather than adopting it, matching its ``login_client_credentials``
1290        posture.
1291
1292        Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response;
1293        ``slow_down`` adds 5 s **permanently**; ``authorization_pending``
1294        loops; ``access_denied`` and ``expired_token`` raise distinct errors;
1295        polling stops at ``expires_in`` even if the server has not yet said
1296        ``expired_token``. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is **not**
1297        terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by
1298        the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the
1299        user has already approved.
1300        """
1301        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1302        authorization = self.device_authorize(
1303            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
1304        )
1305
1306        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
1307        on_user_code(authorization)
1308
1309        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
1310        while True:
1311            if not schedule.tick():
1312                raise self._device_expired_error()
1313            time.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
1314            try:
1315                return self.device_poll(
1316                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
1317                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1318                    configuration=config,
1319                )
1320            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
1321                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
1322                if outcome == "pending" or outcome == "retry":
1323                    continue
1324                if outcome == "slow_down":
1325                    schedule.slow_down()
1326                    continue
1327                raise
1328
1329    def token_exchange(
1330        self,
1331        *,
1332        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
1333        subject_token_type: str,
1334        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
1335        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
1336        audience: str | None = None,
1337        resource: str | None = None,
1338        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1339        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1340    ) -> ExchangedToken:
1341        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (CONTRACT.md §15.1)
1342        — exchange a token for a **narrower** one.
1343
1344        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1345
1346        * **No default ``actor_token``** (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for
1347          *impersonation*; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own
1348          session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
1349        * **No retry or downgrade on ``unauthorized_client``** (rule 2) — a
1350          registration fact an operator must fix.
1351        * **No auto-narrowing on ``invalid_scope``** (rule 3). The server
1352          refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds
1353          out here.
1354        * **No adoption** (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one
1355          outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every
1356          subsequent call this client makes.
1357
1358        A cross-tenant subject token answers ``invalid_grant``, identically to
1359        an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the
1360        server collapses them because distinguishing them is a
1361        tenant-enumeration signal.
1362
1363        Args:
1364            subject_token_type: What kind of token ``subject_token`` is.
1365                ``None`` sends :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE`, the
1366                same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a
1367                **trusted external issuer** (§15.7), set this explicitly —
1368                normally to :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE`. The SDK
1369                never reads ``subject_token`` to decide the value: which kind
1370                of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses
1371                refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry
1372                a refusal as a different type.
1373
1374        Raises:
1375            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1376                with no wire call.
1377        """
1378        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1379        form = self._token_exchange_form(
1380            subject_token=subject_token,
1381            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
1382            actor_token=actor_token,
1383            scopes=scopes,
1384            audience=audience,
1385            resource=resource,
1386        )
1387        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1388        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1389        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1390        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)
1391
1392    def uma_register_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource: ResourceSet) -> ResourceSet:
1393        """``POST /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — register a resource set
1394        (CONTRACT.md §20.1).
1395
1396        The returned ``id`` **is** the AXIAM resource id, directly usable as
1397        the ``resource_id`` of a later :meth:`uma_request_ticket`.
1398        """
1399        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1400            "POST",
1401            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/rreg/resource_set"),
1402            json=self._uma_resource_payload(resource),
1403            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1404        )
1405        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1406        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource registration failed")
1407        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

1410        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — read a resource set (§20.1)."""

1412            "GET",
1413            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
1414            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1415        )
1416        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1417        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource read failed")
1418        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

1420    def uma_update_resource(
1421        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str, resource: ResourceSet
1422    ) -> ResourceSet:
1423        """``PUT /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — replace a resource set (§20.1).

1425        **The scope list is replaced, not merged** (§20.2 rule 8). Whatever
1426        ``resource.resource_scopes`` holds becomes the complete declared set;
1427        omitting a scope removes it, which is how a resource server drops an
1428        authority. This method performs no read-before-write.
1429        """
1430        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1431            "PUT",
1432            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
1433            json=self._uma_resource_payload(resource),
1434            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1435        )
1436        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1437        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource update failed")
1438        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

1440    def uma_delete_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str) -> None:
1441        """``DELETE /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — deregister (§20.1)."""

1443            "DELETE",
1444            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
1445            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1446        )
1447        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1448        self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource delete failed")

1450    def uma_list_resources(self, pat: SecretStr | str) -> list[str]:
1451        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — list the ids **this client**
1452        registered (§20.1).
1453
1454        Not the tenant's whole resource tree: a protection scope does not
1455        entitle a caller to enumerate it.
1456        """
1457        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1458            "GET",
1459            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/rreg/resource_set"),
1460            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1461        )
1462        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1463        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource list failed")
1464        return cast("list[str]", wire or [])

1466    def uma_request_ticket(
1467        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
1468    ) -> SecretStr:
1469        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
1470
1471        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
1472        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
1473        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
1474        server draws rather than flattening it.
1475        """
1476        body = [
1477            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
1478            for p in permissions
1479        ]
1480        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1481            "POST",
1482            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
1483            json=body,
1484            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1485        )
1486        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1487        wire = cast(
1488            "dict[str, str]",
1489            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
1490        )
1491        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])
1492
1493    def uma_exchange_ticket(
1494        self,
1495        *,
1496        ticket: SecretStr | str,
1497        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
1498        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1499        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1500    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
1501        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange
1502        a ticket for an RPT.
1503
1504        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
1505        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
1506        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
1507        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
1508        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the
1509        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
1510        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a
1511        **new** ticket.
1512
1513        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1514
1515        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
1516          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
1517          resource server instead of for the user.
1518        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
1519          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
1520          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
1521        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
1522          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
1523          that user.
1524
1525        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
1526        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
1527        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
1528        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
1529
1530        Raises:
1531            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1532                with no wire call.
1533        """
1534        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1535        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
1536        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1537        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1538        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1539        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)
1540
1541    def logout_url(
1542        self,
1543        *,
1544        id_token: SecretStr | str,
1545        post_logout_redirect_uri: str | None = None,
1546        state: str | None = None,
1547        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1548    ) -> str:
1549        """Build the RP-initiated logout URL to redirect the user agent to
1550        (CONTRACT.md §12.7.2).
1551
1552        Performs **no network I/O** beyond the discovery fetch the SDK caches
1553        anyway, and does **not** clear this client's own session: whether the
1554        local session ends is the application's decision — a backend holding a
1555        service-account session must not lose it because a *user* logged out.
1556
1557        ``end_session_endpoint`` is read from discovery and never synthesised
1558        from the issuer (rule 1). ``post_logout_redirect_uri`` is passed
1559        through unvalidated against any local list (rule 3): the allow-list
1560        lives in the client's server-side registration, and a client-side copy
1561        would drift and reject a URI an operator had just registered.
1562
1563        ``state`` is the caller's to generate and the caller's to check; the
1564        SDK never invents one, because the value only means something to the
1565        application that will receive it back.
1566        """
1567        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1568        return self._logout_url_impl(
1569            config,
1570            id_token=id_token,
1571            post_logout_redirect_uri=post_logout_redirect_uri,
1572            state=state,
1573        )
1574
1575    def verify_logout_token(
1576        self,
1577        token: str,
1578        *,
1579        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1580    ) -> VerifiedLogoutToken:
1581        """Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this
1582        application's ``backchannel_logout_uri`` (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).
1583
1584        Every check exists because skipping it has a name:
1585
1586        1. **Signature**, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token
1587           path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same
1588           ``kid``-required discipline.
1589        2. **``iss``/``aud``**: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
1590        3. **``events`` carries the back-channel-logout key.** This is what
1591           distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means
1592           accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
1593        4. **``nonce`` is absent.** Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it,
1594           and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being
1595           replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
1596        5. **At least one of ``sid``/``sub``** — a token naming neither
1597           identifies nothing.
1598        6. **``exp`` in the future, ``iat`` recent.**
1599
1600        Returns:
1601            The ``sid``/``sub``/``jti`` the token names — never a bare
1602            ``bool``, because the RP has to know *which* session to end.
1603            **Dedup on ``jti`` yourself**: delivery is at-least-once, so a
1604            valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard
1605            would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second
1606            logout after a restart.
1607        """
1608        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1609        return self._verify_logout_token_impl(token, config)
1610
1611    def introspect(
1612        self,
1613        *,
1614        token: SecretStr | str,
1615        token_type_hint: str | None = None,

1617        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1618    ) -> IntrospectionResult:
1619        """``POST /oauth2/introspect`` (RFC 7662, CONTRACT.md §12.1) — ask
1620        the server whether a token is active and, if so, for its metadata.
1621        Requires confidential-client credentials (§12.1 note 4). A ``401``
1622        here is a client-credential failure surfaced as
1623        ``OAuthProtocolError``; it never enters the §9 single-flight
1624        refresh guard (a client-credential failure is not a session
1625        expiry)."""
1626        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1627        form = self._introspect_form(token=token, token_type_hint=token_type_hint)
1628        url = self._endpoint_url_for_introspect(config, tenant_id)
1629        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1630        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1631        return self._handle_introspect_response(response)

1633    def revoke(

1678    def sso_complete(self, *, state: str, code: str) -> SsoCompleteResult:
1679        """``POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/callback`` (CONTRACT.md

1682        ``Set-Cookie`` (§4 cookie jar). §12.4 does not apply here — no ID

1686        )

1693    # Python has no authenticator, so §24.6b's linked-API helper is
1694    # deliberately absent: §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one in software,
1695    # and a "credential" held in process memory is not a second factor. What
1696    # is here is the half that talks to AXIAM, plus §24.6a's JSON bridge —
1697    # which is what lets a Python service be the relying party for a ceremony
1698    # a handset ran.

1706        call** when there is none.

1710        configuration state, not a transient failure, so §24.4 rule 2

1714        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_start")

1731        reaches the server unchanged either way: it is the input to a

1742    def webauthn_authenticate_start(self, *, challenge_token: SecretStr | str) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1743        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).

1747        ``challenge_token`` is that result's ``mfa_token``.

1750        one with an optional argument — see §24.2 for why they cannot be

1760    def webauthn_authenticate_finish(

1763        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).

1766        "MAY adopt" posture: ``device_login`` mints tokens a caller may want to
1767        route elsewhere, and this is the SDK's own primary authentication —

1777    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:

1781        an empty ``allowCredentials``, and the assertion itself identifies the
1782        user. The workspace still has to be named — a discoverable credential

1794    def webauthn_discoverable_finish(
1795        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1796    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1797        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1798
1799        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3). Unlike its username-bound
1800        twin, this fires the server's ``login.post_auth`` reactor hook (§22.5):
1801        there was no password step for the event to have been fired at.

1807    def _webauthn_finish_sync(
1808        self,
1809        path: str,
1810        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1811        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1812        operation: str,
1813    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1814        """The shared tail of both authentication ceremonies."""
1815        self._ensure_open()
1816        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
1817        # this call changes the subject.
1818        self._on_credential_change()
1819        body = self._webauthn_finish_body(state_token, response, operation)
1820        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1821        http_response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1822        result = self._webauthn_login_result(http_response, operation)
1823        # The server sets the same axiam_access/axiam_refresh/axiam_csrf triple
1824        # here as it does on a password login, so adoption is the same call.
1825        self._absorb_session_cookies()
1826        return result

1900    def resend_verification(self, *, email: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1901        """``POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the
1902        **unauthenticated** resend, for a caller with no session.
1903
1904        **Returns normally whatever the outcome.** The address may not exist,
1905        may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this
1906        answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an
1907        anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have
1908        accounts (§25.7).
1909
1910        A caller that *is* signed in wants :meth:`resend_own_verification`,
1911        which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it
1912        is the name you already knew.
1913        """
1914        self._ensure_open()
1915        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1916            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_VERIFICATION, json={"email": email, "tenant_id": tenant_id}
1917        )
1918        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "resend_verification")
1919
1920    def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1921        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1922        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1923        and say what happened.
1924
1925        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1926        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1927        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1928        address.
1929
1930        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1931        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1932        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1933
1934        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1935          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1936          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1937          succeeding.
1938        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1939          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1940        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1941
1942        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1943        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1944        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1945        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1946        """
1947        self._ensure_open()
1948        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1949            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1950        )
1951        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "resend_own_verification")

1965        exposes no way to tell the two apart. That is not an omission to
1966        improve on: a client that surfaced a "no such user" state — even one
1967        inferred from timing — would turn the endpoint into the account
1968        enumeration oracle its uniform response exists to prevent (§25.4).

1972            email=email, org_slug=org_slug, tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_slug=tenant_slug
1973        )

1975        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "request_password_reset")

1977    def password_reset_context(self, *, token: SecretStr | str) -> PasswordResetContext:
1978        """``GET /api/v1/auth/reset/context`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the OPAQUE
1979        policy for the account a reset token belongs to.

1981        Call this before :meth:`confirm_password_reset` on any tenant that
1982        might have §23 enabled: the client has to build a registration record,

The AXIAM SDK's sync REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10).

client.login(...) returns a typed ~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult with mfa_required (SC#1). For the async twin, use ~axiam_sdk.AsyncAxiamClient (SDK-Q08) — a separate class, not an async_* method on this one.

def close(self) -> None: 
683    def close(self) -> None:
684        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
685
686        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
687        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
688
689        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
690        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
691        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
692        restart and resume; a ``close()`` that logged out would silently end
693        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
694        ending the session is what you want.
695
696        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
697        rather than silently reconnecting.
698        """
699        self._closed = True
700        self._decision_memo.clear()
701        self._session.close()

def login_opaque( self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult: 
719    def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
720        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
721
722        Returns the same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
723        ``mfa_required`` case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.
724
725        What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither
726        useful without the account's registration record **and** the tenant's
727        OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request
728        log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password,
729        because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database
730        is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not
731        offer. It does **not** protect against a compromised AXIAM server.
732
733        Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server
734        proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the
735        server during the handshake, so opening ``KE2`` *is* the proof that it
736        holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an ``M2`` check in
737        capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now
738        nothing to skip.
739
740        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
741            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
742            SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not ``AuthError``: reporting a
743            configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to
744            reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to
745            :meth:`login`.
746        :raises AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist,
747            an account with no registration record, and a server that does not
748            hold the record — indistinguishable by design. **Nothing is sent to
749            ``login/finish`` in that case** (§23.4 rule 7).
750
751        **The ``mode`` field decides what happens after a failed exchange**, and
752        nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). ``login/start`` carries the tenant's
753        ``opaque_mode``:
754
755        * ``"optional"`` — this method retries over :meth:`login` with the same
756          credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's
757          outcome. Under ``optional`` an account with no record is the ordinary
758          case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an
759          operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a
760          password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every
761          user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state ``optional`` exists
762          to serve.
763        * ``"required"``, an unrecognised value, or **no ``mode`` at all** (a
764          server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is
765          retried over :meth:`login`. It would be refused anyway: ``required``
766          answers ``403 opaque_required`` for every principal in the tenant, so
767          trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.
768
769        ``mode`` is **not** downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a
770        hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer ``404`` and get
771        the fallback whatever it puts here. ``required`` is what closes that,
772        server-side, by refusing ``/auth/login`` before examining any
773        credential.
774
775        This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by
776        default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is
777        the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by
778        someone holding the OPRF seed.
779        """
780        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
781
782        self._ensure_open()
783        self._on_credential_change()
784
785        exchange = start_login(password)
786
787        # One round trip, always. SRP had to guess a group before the server
788        # named one and restart the exchange if it guessed wrong; ``KE1`` does
789        # not depend on the KSF.
790        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
791            "POST",
792            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
793            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
794        )
795        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
796        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
797            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
798        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
799
800        try:
801            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
802        except AuthError:
803            # §23.4 rule 7. `KE3` is not sent either way; `mode` — and only
804            # `mode` — decides whether the plaintext path may be tried.
805            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
806                raise
807            return self.login(username_or_email, password)
808
809        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
810            "POST",
811            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
812            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
813        )
814        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
815        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
816            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
817        return self._handle_login_response(response)

OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.

Returns the same LoginResult as login(), including the mfa_required case, so a caller needs one result handler for both.

What crosses the wire is a blinded group element and a MAC, neither useful without the account's registration record and the tenant's OPRF seed — so a TLS-terminating proxy, an accidentally verbose request log, or a heap dump on the server cannot capture a plaintext password, because the server never has one. It also means a stolen record database is not offline-crackable on its own, which is the property SRP could not offer. It does not protect against a compromised AXIAM server.

Unlike its SRP predecessor this returns without verifying a server proof, and there is nothing missing: RFC 9807's AKE authenticates the server during the handshake, so opening KE2 is the proof that it holds the record. §23.3 rule 6 had to mandate an M2 check in capitals because skipping it kept only half the protocol; there is now nothing to skip.

Raises
  • NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this SDK cannot perform. Deliberately not AuthError: reporting a configuration gap as a credential failure would send a user off to reset a working password, and would stop a caller falling back to login().
  • AuthError: for a wrong password, an account that does not exist, an account with no registration record, and a server that does not hold the record — indistinguishable by design. Nothing is sent to login/finish in that case (§23.4 rule 7).

The mode field decides what happens after a failed exchange, and nothing else does (§23.4 rule 7). login/start carries the tenant's opaque_mode:

  • "optional" — this method retries over login() with the same credentials before reporting anything, and returns that call's outcome. Under optional an account with no record is the ordinary case rather than an error: every account has none the moment an operator enables OPAQUE, and they acquire one only as they next set a password. Treating the failed exchange as final would lock out every user of a tenant mid-migration, which is the state optional exists to serve.
  • "required", an unrecognised value, or no mode at all (a server older than the field) — the failure is final and nothing is retried over login(). It would be refused anyway: required answers 403 opaque_required for every principal in the tenant, so trying would put a plaintext password on the wire for nothing.

mode is not downgrade protection and must not be read as such: a hostile server that wanted the plaintext could answer 404 and get the fallback whatever it puts here. required is what closes that, server-side, by refusing /auth/login before examining any credential.

This runs the tenant's key-stretching function: Argon2id at 19 MiB by default, tens to hundreds of milliseconds of blocking work. That cost is the point — it is what makes a stolen record expensive to attack even by someone holding the OPRF seed.

def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
819    def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
820        """Build a registration record to send with any request that sets a
821        password (user creation, change-password, reset completion).
822
823        The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to
824        arrive with the request or not at all.
825
826        Performs a ``register/start`` round trip, which the SRP verifier this
827        replaces did not need: OPAQUE's envelope is sealed under the server's
828        oblivious PRF, so there is no offline computation that produces a valid
829        record.
830
831        Note the absence of an ``identity`` argument. The SRP version required
832        the account's canonical username, and passing an email produced a
833        verifier no login could ever satisfy. A record binds to a credential
834        identifier the server chooses, so there is nothing here to get wrong.
835
836        :raises NetworkError: when the tenant has OPAQUE disabled, when the
837            shared library is not installed, or when the server names a KSF this
838            SDK cannot perform.
839        """
840        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
841
842        self._ensure_open()
843        exchange = start_registration(password)
844
845        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
846            "POST",
847            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
848            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request),
849        )
850        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
851        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
852            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
853        started = response.json()
854
855        return {
856            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
857            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
858                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
859            ),
860        }

The server cannot build one — it never sees the plaintext — so it has to arrive with the request or not at all.

def refresh(self) -> None: 
878    def refresh(self) -> None:
879        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
880        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
881        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
882        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
883        self._ensure_open()
884        self._on_credential_change()
885        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
886        if not observed_access:
887            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
888
889        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
890        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
891        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
892        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
893        self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_sync(
894            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_sync(tenant_id, org_id)
895        )

def check_access( self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None, *, subject_id: str | None = None) -> AccessResult: 
933    def check_access(
934        self,
935        action: str,
936        resource_id: str,
937        scope: str | None = None,
938        *,
939        subject_id: str | None = None,
940    ) -> AccessResult:
941        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
942
943        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
944        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
945        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
946        declarative ``require_access`` helpers (§11) pass to check the
947        *request's* authenticated user.
948        """
949        self._ensure_open()
950        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
951        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
952        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
953        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
954        if memoized is not None:
955            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
956            return memoized
957
958        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
959        wire = self._authz_post_sync(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
960        result = AccessResult(**wire)
961
962        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
963        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
964        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
965        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
966        return result
