def oidc_par( self, *, request: AuthorizationRequest, redirect_uri: str, scope: str | list[str] | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest: 
1079    def oidc_par(
1080        self,
1081        *,
1082        request: AuthorizationRequest,
1083        redirect_uri: str,
1084        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
1085        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1086        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1087    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
1088        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
1089        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
1090        with.
1091
1092        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
1093        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
1094        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
1095        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
1096        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
1097        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
1098
1099        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
1100        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
1101        authorize any other way (§21.1).
1102
1103        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
1104        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
1105
1106        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
1107        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
1108        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
1109        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
1110
1111        Raises:
1112            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
1113                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
1114            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
1115        """
1116        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1117        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
1118        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
1119        http_request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1120        response = self._session._send_sync(http_request)
1121        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)

POST /oauth2/par (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect with.

PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting scope, redirect_uri, state and the PKCE challenge into a URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque request_uri in the redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

Required for a FAPI 2.0 client — profile: "fapi2" refuses a registration that does not set require_par, so such a client cannot authorize any other way (§21.1).

A §12 extension, not a replacement: oidc_exchange afterwards is unchanged, and takes the code_verifier carried on the result.

Not retried on a 5xx or a transport failure — it is a POST that creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only eligibility exactly as oidc_exchange does. The safe recovery is a fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).

Raises: AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. OAuthProtocolError: on any error the server returns.

def oidc_refresh( self, *, refresh_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
1149    def oidc_refresh(
1150        self,
1151        *,
1152        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
1153        scope: str | None = None,
1154        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1155        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1156    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
1157        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
1158        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
1159
1160        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
1161        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
1162        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
1163        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
1164        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
1165        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
1166        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
1167        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
1168        interleave.
1169        """
1170
1171        def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
1172            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
1173            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_sync`
1174            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
1175            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
1176            config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1177            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
1178            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1179            request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1180            response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1181            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
1182            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
1183
1184        def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
1185            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
1186            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
1187            :meth:`refresh` call."""
1188            token_set: OidcTokenSet = self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_sync(do_refresh)
1189            return token_set
1190
1191        result: OidcTokenSet = self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_sync.run(under_guard)
1192        return result

1280        user code, poll to completion.
1281
1282        ``on_user_code`` is called with the :class:`DeviceAuthorization`
1283        **before the first poll** — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have
1284        had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK
1285        never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink
1286        panel) is the application's decision.
1287
1288        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
1289        set rather than adopting it, matching its ``login_client_credentials``
1290        posture.
1291
1292        Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response;
1293        ``slow_down`` adds 5 s **permanently**; ``authorization_pending``
1294        loops; ``access_denied`` and ``expired_token`` raise distinct errors;
1295        polling stops at ``expires_in`` even if the server has not yet said
1296        ``expired_token``. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is **not**
1297        terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by
1298        the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the
1299        user has already approved.
1300        """
1301        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1302        authorization = self.device_authorize(
1303            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
1304        )
1305
1306        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
1307        on_user_code(authorization)
1308
1309        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
1310        while True:
1311            if not schedule.tick():
1312                raise self._device_expired_error()
1313            time.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
1314            try:
1315                return self.device_poll(
1316                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
1317                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
1318                    configuration=config,
1319                )
1320            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
1321                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
1322                if outcome == "pending" or outcome == "retry":
1323                    continue
1324                if outcome == "slow_down":
1325                    schedule.slow_down()
1326                    continue
1327                raise

The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the user code, poll to completion.

on_user_code is called with the DeviceAuthorization before the first poll — §14.3 rule 2 requires the caller to have had the chance to display the code before polling begins. The SDK never prints it: what the device does with it (screen, QR code, e-ink panel) is the application's decision.

Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK returns the token set rather than adopting it, matching its login_client_credentials posture.

Polling follows §14.2: the interval comes from the response; slow_down adds 5 s permanently; authorization_pending loops; access_denied and expired_token raise distinct errors; polling stops at expires_in even if the server has not yet said expired_token. A 5xx or transport failure mid-poll is not terminal (rule 6) — the loop absorbs it and tries again, bounded by the same deadline, because a server restart must not lose a grant the user has already approved.

1348          session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.

1352          refuses instead of silently narrowing precisely so the caller finds
1353          out here.

1355          outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every
1356          subsequent call this client makes.

1359        an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the
1360        server collapses them because distinguishing them is a
1361        tenant-enumeration signal.
1362
1363        Args:
1364            subject_token_type: What kind of token ``subject_token`` is.
1365                ``None`` sends :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE`, the
1366                same-domain exchange of §15.1. To exchange a token from a
1367                **trusted external issuer** (§15.7), set this explicitly —
1368                normally to :data:`~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE`. The SDK
1369                never reads ``subject_token`` to decide the value: which kind
1370                of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses
1371                refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry
1372                a refusal as a different type.

1375            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1376                with no wire call.

1380            subject_token=subject_token,
1381            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
1382            actor_token=actor_token,
1383            scopes=scopes,
1384            audience=audience,
1385            resource=resource,
1386        )
1387        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1388        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1389        response = self._session._send_sync(request)

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default actor_token (§15.2 rule 1). Passing none asks for impersonation; the SDK will not quietly reuse the client's own session token as the actor and turn that into a delegation.
  • No retry or downgrade on unauthorized_client (rule 2) — a registration fact an operator must fix.

  • No adoption (rule 5). The returned token is handed onward in one outbound call; adopting it would silently re-privilege every subsequent call this client makes.

A cross-tenant subject token answers invalid_grant, identically to an expired one. The SDK does not try to tell them apart (§15.3): the server collapses them because distinguishing them is a tenant-enumeration signal.

To exchange a token from a trusted external issuer (§15.7), set this explicitly — normally to ~axiam_sdk._oidc.JWT_TOKEN_TYPE. The SDK never reads subject_token to decide the value: which kind of token you hold is something only you know, AXIAM refuses refresh and ID token types by name, and the SDK will not retry a refusal as a different type.

def uma_request_ticket( self, pat: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]) -> pydantic.types.SecretStr: 
1466    def uma_request_ticket(
1467        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
1468    ) -> SecretStr:
1469        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
1470
1471        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
1472        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
1473        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
1474        server draws rather than flattening it.
1475        """
1476        body = [
1477            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
1478            for p in permissions
1479        ]
1480        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1481            "POST",
1482            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
1483            json=body,
1484            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
1485        )
1486        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1487        wire = cast(
1488            "dict[str, str]",
1489            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
1490        )
1491        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])

1494        self,
1495        *,
1496        ticket: SecretStr | str,
1497        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
1498        tenant_id: str | None = None,

1501        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange
1502        a ticket for an RPT.

1505        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
1506        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
1507        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
1508        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the
1509        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
1510        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a
1511        **new** ticket.
1512
1513        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
1514

1516          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
1517          resource server instead of for the user.
1518        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
1519          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
1520          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
1521        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
1522          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
1523          that user.
1524
1525        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
1526        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
1527        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
1528        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
1529
1530        Raises:
1531            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
1532                with no wire call.
1533        """
1534        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1535        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
1536        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
1537        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
1538        response = self._session._send_sync(request)
1539        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)

POST /oauth2/token with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a ticket for an RPT.

This method never retries. It issues exactly one request and is outside the §16 retry policy — not on 5xx, not on timeout, not on any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed before the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a new ticket.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default claim_token (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the resource server instead of for the user.
  • No auto-narrowing on access_denied (rule 3). A partial grant is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the application's judgement, not this SDK's.
  • No adoption (rule 4). The RPT is the requesting party's token. Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as that user.

The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client — all answer invalid_grant with one message. This SDK does not try to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller cannot probe for live ticket handles.

Raises: AuthError: when no client_secret was configured — client-side, with no wire call.

def verify_logout_token( self, token: str, *, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> VerifiedLogoutToken: 
1575    def verify_logout_token(
1576        self,
1577        token: str,
1578        *,
1579        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
1580    ) -> VerifiedLogoutToken:
1581        """Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this
1582        application's ``backchannel_logout_uri`` (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).
1583
1584        Every check exists because skipping it has a name:
1585
1586        1. **Signature**, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token
1587           path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same
1588           ``kid``-required discipline.
1589        2. **``iss``/``aud``**: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
1590        3. **``events`` carries the back-channel-logout key.** This is what
1591           distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means
1592           accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
1593        4. **``nonce`` is absent.** Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it,
1594           and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being
1595           replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
1596        5. **At least one of ``sid``/``sub``** — a token naming neither
1597           identifies nothing.
1598        6. **``exp`` in the future, ``iat`` recent.**
1599
1600        Returns:
1601            The ``sid``/``sub``/``jti`` the token names — never a bare
1602            ``bool``, because the RP has to know *which* session to end.
1603            **Dedup on ``jti`` yourself**: delivery is at-least-once, so a
1604            valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard
1605            would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second
1606            logout after a restart.
1607        """
1608        config = configuration or self.oidc_discover()
1609        return self._verify_logout_token_impl(token, config)

Verify a back-channel logout token the OP POSTed to this application's backchannel_logout_uri (CONTRACT.md §12.7.3).

Every check exists because skipping it has a name:

  1. Signature, through the same §12.4 JWKS verifier the ID-token path uses — no second key-fetching path — with the same kid-required discipline.
  2. iss/aud: a token minted for another RP is not accepted.
  3. events carries the back-channel-logout key. This is what distinguishes a logout token from an ID token; skipping it means accepting a replayed ID token as a logout instruction.
  4. nonce is absent. Back-Channel Logout 1.0 §2.4 forbids it, and its presence is the documented signature of an ID token being replayed. Rejected, not ignored.
  5. At least one of sid/sub — a token naming neither identifies nothing.
  6. exp in the future, iat recent.

Returns: The sid/sub/jti the token names — never a bare bool, because the RP has to know which session to end. Dedup on jti yourself: delivery is at-least-once, so a valid token legitimately arrives twice, and an SDK-side guard would have no durable store and would silently drop a real second logout after a restart.

def resend_own_verification(self) -> None: 
1920    def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1921        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1922        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1923        and say what happened.
1924
1925        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1926        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1927        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1928        address.
1929
1930        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1931        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1932        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1933
1934        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1935          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1936          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1937          succeeding.
1938        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1939          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1940        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1941
1942        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1943        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1944        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1945        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1946        """
1947        self._ensure_open()
1948        request = self._session.sync_client.build_request(
1949            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1950        )
1951        self._expect_no_content(self._session._send_sync(request), "resend_own_verification")

POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification (CONTRACT.md §25.1, §25.7) — resend the signed-in caller's own verification mail, and say what happened.

Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary address.

Unlike resend_verification() this reports the outcome, because the caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:

  • returns — a token was minted and the mail enqueued. Delivery is asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this succeeding.
  • ~axiam_sdk.ConflictError (from 409) — already verified, or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
  • ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError (from 429) — the daily limit.

§25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.

  81    :class:`~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult` with ``mfa_required`` (SC#1) — the
  82    same contract as the sync :class:`~axiam_sdk.AxiamClient`, on its own
  83    dedicated async object. Constructing both an ``AxiamClient`` and an
  84    ``AsyncAxiamClient`` against the same ``base_url``/``tenant_slug`` gives
  85    each its own independent ``_Session`` (cookie jar, CSRF state, refresh
  86    guard) — the two classes do NOT share session state with each other, only
  87    each shares consistently within its own sync or async call path.
  88    """
  89
  90    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  91    # Lifecycle (D-19)
  92    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  93
  94    async def __aenter__(self) -> AsyncAxiamClient:
  95        """Async context-manager entry — returns ``self`` (D-19); no
  96        separate setup beyond what ``__init__`` already did."""
  97        return self
  98
  99    async def __aexit__(self, *exc_info: object) -> None:
 100        """Async context-manager exit — always calls :meth:`aclose`,
 101        regardless of whether the ``async with`` block raised (D-19)."""
 102        await self.aclose()
 103
 104    async def aclose(self) -> None:
 105        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
 106
 107        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
 108        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
 109
 110        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
 111        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
 112        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
 113        restart and resume; an ``aclose()`` that logged out would silently end
 114        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
 115        ending the session is what you want.
 116
 117        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
 118        rather than silently reconnecting.
 119        """
 120        self._closed = True
 121        self._decision_memo.clear()
 122        await self._session.aclose()
 123
 124    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 125    # login / verify_mfa
 126    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 127
 128    async def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 129        """``POST /api/v1/auth/login`` (CONTRACT.md §1). Returns a typed
 130        :class:`LoginResult`; check ``mfa_required`` before assuming the
 131        session is established (SC#1)."""
 132        self._ensure_open()
 133        self._on_credential_change()
 134        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 135            "POST", LOGIN_PATH, json=self._login_body(email, password)
 136        )
 137        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 138        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 139
 140    async def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
 141        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
 142
 143        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.login_opaque`; see that method for
 144        the full contract — including what the ``login/start`` response's
 145        ``mode`` field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under
 146        ``"optional"`` this retries over :meth:`login` and returns that call's
 147        outcome, and under ``"required"``, an unrecognised value or no ``mode``
 148        at all it raises :class:`AuthError` and retries nothing. Returns the
 149        same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
 150        ``mfa_required`` case.
 151
 152        The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it:
 153        Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a
 154        server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in
 155        :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
 156        """
 157        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
 158
 159        self._ensure_open()
 160        self._on_credential_change()
 161
 162        exchange = start_login(password)
 163
 164        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 165            "POST",
 166            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
 167            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
 168        )
 169        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 170        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 171            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
 172        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
 173
 174        try:
 175            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
 176        except AuthError:
 177            # §23.4 rule 7, decided identically to the sync client — the shared
 178            # `allows_password_fallback` is what keeps the two from drifting.
 179            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
 180                raise
 181            return await self.login(username_or_email, password)
 182
 183        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 184            "POST",
 185            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
 186            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
 187        )
 188        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 189        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
 190            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
 191        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 192
 193    async def opaque_enrollment(self, password: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 194        """Build a registration record for *password*.
 195
 196        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.opaque_enrollment`; see that method
 197        for the full contract.
 198        """
 199        from ._opaque import KsfParams, start_registration
 200
 201        self._ensure_open()
 202        exchange = start_registration(password)
 203
 204        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 205            "POST",
 206            OPAQUE_REGISTER_START_PATH,
 207            json=self._opaque_register_start_body(exchange.request),
 208        )
 209        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 210        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 211            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "register/start")
 212        started = response.json()
 213
 214        return {
 215            "opaque_session": started["opaque_session"],
 216            "registration_record": exchange.finish(
 217                password, started["registration_response"], KsfParams.from_wire(started)
 218            ),
 219        }
 220
 221    async def verify_mfa(self, mfa_token: Any, code: str) -> LoginResult:
 222        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — completes the
 223        two-phase flow started by :meth:`login` when ``mfa_required`` was
 224        true."""
 225        self._ensure_open()
 226        self._on_credential_change()
 227        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 228            "POST", MFA_VERIFY_PATH, json=self._mfa_verify_body(mfa_token, code)
 229        )
 230        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 231        return self._handle_login_response(response)
 232
 233    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 234    # refresh — exactly one literal /api/v1/auth/refresh POST, routed
 235    # through the single-flight guard (Pitfall 4, §9.3)
 236    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 237
 238    async def refresh(self) -> None:
 239        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
 240        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
 241        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
 242        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
 243        self._ensure_open()
 244        self._on_credential_change()
 245        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
 246        if not observed_access:
 247            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
 248
 249        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
 250        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
 251        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
 252        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
 253        await self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_async(
 254            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_async(tenant_id, org_id)
 255        )
 256
 257    async def _do_refresh_async(self, tenant_id: str, org_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
 258        """Perform the actual ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` call — the
 259        ``do_refresh`` closure passed to
 260        :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.refresh_if_needed_async`
 261        by :meth:`refresh`. Not called directly by SDK users; always routed
 262        through the single-flight guard so concurrent 401s collapse into
 263        one in-flight call (§9)."""
 264        # The literal /api/v1/auth/refresh path is required so the
 265        # Path-scoped axiam_refresh cookie attaches (Pitfall 4).
 266        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 267            "POST", "/api/v1/auth/refresh", json=self._refresh_body(tenant_id, org_id)
 268        )
 269        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 270        return self._handle_refresh_response(response)
 271
 272    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 273    # logout
 274    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 275
 276    async def logout(self) -> None:
 277        """``POST /api/v1/auth/logout`` (CONTRACT.md §1)."""
 278        self._ensure_open()
 279        self._on_credential_change()
 280        session_id = self._session_id_for_logout()
 281        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 282            "POST", LOGOUT_PATH, json={"session_id": session_id}
 283        )
 284        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 285        if response.status_code >= 300:
 286            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "logout failed", response=response)
 287        self._session.refresh_guard = type(self._session.refresh_guard)()
 288
 289    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 290    # REST authz: check_access / can / batch_check
 291    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 292
 293    async def check_access(
 294        self,
 295        action: str,
 296        resource_id: str,
 297        scope: str | None = None,
 298        *,
 299        subject_id: str | None = None,
 300    ) -> AccessResult:
 301        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
 302
 303        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
 304        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
 305        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
 306        declarative ``require_access`` helper (§11) passes to check the
 307        *request's* authenticated user rather than this client's own
 308        (often service-account) session.
 309        """
 310        self._ensure_open()
 311        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
 312        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
 313        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 314        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
 315        if memoized is not None:
 316            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
 317            return memoized
 318
 319        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
 320        wire = await self._authz_post_async(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
 321        result = AccessResult(**wire)
 322
 323        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
 324        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
 325        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
 326        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
 327        return result
 328
 329    async def can(self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None) -> bool:
 330        """Alias for ``check_access`` returning only the allowed boolean
 331        (CONTRACT.md §1 note, browser/UI scenarios)."""
 332        result = await self.check_access(action, resource_id, scope)
 333        return result.allowed
 334
 335    async def batch_check(self, checks: list[AccessCheck]) -> list[AccessResult]:
 336        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check/batch`` (CONTRACT.md §1) — results
 337        returned in the same order as ``checks``."""
 338        body = {"checks": [c.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for c in checks]}
 339        wire = await self._authz_post_async(BATCH_CHECK_PATH, body, operation="batch_check")
 340        return BatchCheckResult(**wire).results
 341
 342    async def _authz_post_async(
 343        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], *, operation: str
 344    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 345        """POST an authz request body to *path* under the §16 retry policy.
 346
 347        The call is a ``POST`` but changes no server state, so it is
 348        retry-eligible: §16.2's test is "changes no server state", NOT "is a
 349        GET". Gating on the verb would exclude the single most important
 350        operation this policy covers.
 351
 352        The §9.3 refresh-then-retry-once on a 401 is a *different* mechanism and
 353        stays inside one §16 attempt: a 401 means the token expired, which
 354        refreshing fixes, and neither backing off nor counting it against the
 355        transport-failure budget would make sense.
 356        """
 357        return await retry_async(
 358            lambda attempt: self._authz_post_async_once(path, body, operation, attempt),
 359            operation=operation,
 360            enabled=self._retry_enabled,
 361            telemetry=self._telemetry,
 362        )
 363
 364    async def _authz_post_async_once(
 365        self, path: str, body: dict[str, Any], operation: str, attempt: int
 366    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
 367        """One §16 attempt, with its §19 request pair."""
 368        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
 369        with self._telemetry.request(operation, "POST", path, attempt) as span:
 370            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 371
 372            if response.status_code == httpx.codes.UNAUTHORIZED:
 373                response = await self._retry_after_refresh_async(request)
 374
 375            span.status = response.status_code
 376            if response.status_code < 200 or response.status_code >= 300:
 377                raise error_from_http_status(
 378                    response.status_code, "authz check failed", response=response
 379                )
 380            span.outcome = "success"
 381            result: dict[str, Any] = response.json()
 382            return result
 383
 384    async def _retry_after_refresh_async(self, original_request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
 385        """On a 401, refresh exactly once (via the shared single-flight
 386        guard) then retry the failed authz call exactly once. A second
 387        failure propagates through the caller's own status check (§9.3, no
 388        retry loop)."""
 389        await self.refresh()
 390        retry_request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 391            original_request.method,
 392            original_request.url,
 393            content=original_request.content,
 394            headers={
 395                k: v
 396                for k, v in original_request.headers.items()
 397                if k.lower() not in ("content-length", "x-csrf-token")
 398            },
 399        )
 400        return await self._session._send_async(retry_request)
 401
 402    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 403    # OIDC / SSO relying-party helpers (CONTRACT.md §12, Task T3, SDK-Q08)
 404    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 405
 406    async def oidc_discover(self) -> OidcConfiguration:
 407        """``GET /.well-known/openid-configuration`` (CONTRACT.md §12.1) —
 408        fetch the OIDC discovery document, cached per origin with a
 409        ≥5-minute TTL and single-flight de-duplication of concurrent calls
 410        (§12.3 rule 6)."""
 411
 412        async def fetch() -> OidcConfiguration:
 413            """Perform the actual discovery-document GET; called by the
 414            discovery cache at most once per cache miss/expiry."""
 415            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("GET", DISCOVERY_PATH)
 416            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 417            return self._parse_discovery_response(response)
 418
 419        return await self._discovery_cache.get_async(self._discovery_origin_key(), fetch)
 420
 421    async def oidc_begin(
 422        self,
 423        *,
 424        configuration: OidcConfiguration,
 425        redirect_uri: str,
 426        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
 427        extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
 428    ) -> AuthorizationRequest:
 429        """Build an authorization request (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — **pure
 430        local computation, no network I/O**; this ``async def`` has no
 431        internal ``await`` (CONTRACT.md §12.2's Python naming table gives
 432        ``oidc_begin`` no synchronous carve-out the way it does for C#).
 433        Nothing is stored: persist the returned ``state``, ``nonce``, and
 434        ``code_verifier`` yourself (§12.3 rule 1)."""
 435        return self._oidc_begin_impl(
 436            configuration=configuration,
 437            redirect_uri=redirect_uri,
 438            scope=scope,
 439            extra_params=extra_params,
 440        )
 441
 442    async def oidc_par(
 443        self,
 444        *,
 445        request: AuthorizationRequest,
 446        redirect_uri: str,
 447        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
 448        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 449        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 450    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
 451        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
 452        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
 453        with.
 454
 455        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
 456        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
 457        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
 458        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
 459        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
 460        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
 461
 462        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
 463        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
 464        authorize any other way (§21.1).
 465
 466        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
 467        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
 468
 469        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
 470        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
 471        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
 472        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
 473
 474        Raises:
 475            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
 476                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
 477            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
 478        """
 479        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 480        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
 481        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
 482        http_request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 483        response = await self._session._send_async(http_request)
 484        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)
 485
 486    async def oidc_exchange(
 487        self,
 488        *,
 489        code: str,
 490        code_verifier: SecretStr | str,
 491        redirect_uri: str,
 492        nonce: str,
 493        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 494        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 495    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 496        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=authorization_code``
 497        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — exchange an authorization code for a token
 498        set, validating the returned ID token in full before returning
 499        (§12.4). On ANY §12.4 failure the whole token set is discarded and
 500        ``AuthError`` is raised with the matching reason code (§12.4
 501        rule 7) — the access/refresh token from the same response is never
 502        returned."""
 503        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 504        form = self._exchange_form(
 505            code=code, code_verifier=code_verifier, redirect_uri=redirect_uri
 506        )
 507        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 508        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 509        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 510        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, nonce)
 511
 512    async def oidc_refresh(
 513        self,
 514        *,
 515        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
 516        scope: str | None = None,
 517        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 518        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 519    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 520        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
 521        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
 522
 523        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
 524        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
 525        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
 526        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
 527        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
 528        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
 529        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
 530        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
 531        interleave.
 532        """
 533
 534        async def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
 535            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
 536            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_async`
 537            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
 538            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
 539            config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 540            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
 541            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 542            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 543            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 544            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
 545            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 546
 547        async def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
 548            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
 549            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
 550            :meth:`refresh` call."""
 551            token_set: OidcTokenSet = await self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_async(
 552                do_refresh
 553            )
 554            return token_set
 555
 556        result: OidcTokenSet = await self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_async.run(under_guard)
 557        return result
 558
 559    async def login_client_credentials(
 560        self,
 561        *,
 562        scope: str | None = None,
 563        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 564        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 565    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 566        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=client_credentials``
 567        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — service-account machine-to-machine login.
 568        Requests no ``openid`` scope, so the response carries no
 569        ``id_token``.
 570
 571        Raises:
 572            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — this
 573                grant cannot be performed by a public client.
 574        """
 575        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 576        form = self._client_credentials_form(scope=scope)
 577        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 578        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 579        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 580        # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to this grant.
 581        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 582
 583    async def device_authorize(
 584        self,
 585        *,
 586        scope: str | None = None,
 587        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 588        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 589    ) -> DeviceAuthorization:
 590        """``POST /oauth2/device_authorization`` (CONTRACT.md §14.1) — start
 591        the device grant and obtain the code pair.
 592
 593        **Unauthenticated by design**: a device that cannot show a browser also
 594        cannot hold a client secret, so this never sends ``client_secret`` and
 595        never refuses a client built without one.
 596
 597        Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.device_authorize`; §14.4
 598        requires the same three names on both clients.
 599        """
 600        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 601        form = self._device_authorize_form(scope=scope)
 602        url = self._device_authorization_url(config, tenant_id)
 603        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 604        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 605        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
 606            raise error_from_oauth2_response(
 607                response.status_code, response, "device authorization request failed"
 608            )
 609        return self._build_device_authorization(response.json())
 610
 611    async def device_poll(
 612        self,
 613        *,
 614        device_code: SecretStr | str,
 615        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 616        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 617    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 618        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the device-code grant (§14.1) — **one**
 619        poll attempt.
 620
 621        The five RFC 8628 §3.5 answers surface as ``OAuthProtocolError``,
 622        ``authorization_pending`` and ``slow_down`` included, so a hand-rolled
 623        loop sees exactly what :meth:`device_login` sees.
 624        """
 625        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 626        form = self._device_poll_form(device_code=device_code)
 627        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 628        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 629        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 630        return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
 631
 632    async def device_login(
 633        self,
 634        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]],
 635        *,
 636        scope: str | None = None,
 637        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 638        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 639    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
 640        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
 641        user code, poll to completion.
 642
 643        ``on_user_code`` is invoked — and **awaited when it returns an
 644        awaitable** — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering
 645        a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves
 646        would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.
 647
 648        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
 649        set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync
 650        twin's docstring for the full rule set.
 651        """
 652        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 653        authorization = await self.device_authorize(
 654            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
 655        )
 656
 657        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
 658        result = on_user_code(authorization)
 659        if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
 660            await result
 661
 662        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
 663        while True:
 664            if not schedule.tick():
 665                raise self._device_expired_error()
 666            await asyncio.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
 667            try:
 668                return await self.device_poll(
 669                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
 670                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
 671                    configuration=config,
 672                )
 673            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
 674                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
 675                if outcome in ("pending", "retry"):
 676                    continue
 677                if outcome == "slow_down":
 678                    schedule.slow_down()
 679                    continue
 680                raise
 681
 682    async def token_exchange(
 683        self,
 684        *,
 685        subject_token: SecretStr | str,
 686        subject_token_type: str,
 687        actor_token: SecretStr | str | None = None,
 688        scopes: Sequence[str] | None = None,
 689        audience: str | None = None,
 690        resource: str | None = None,
 691        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 692        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 693    ) -> ExchangedToken:
 694        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with the RFC 8693 grant (§15.1) — exchange a
 695        token for a **narrower** one.
 696
 697        Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.token_exchange`; see that
 698        docstring for what this method deliberately refuses to do (no
 699        defaulted ``actor_token``, no auto-narrowing, no adoption) and for
 700        ``subject_token_type``, which reaches the external exchange of §15.7
 701        and is never inferred from the token.
 702        """
 703        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 704        form = self._token_exchange_form(
 705            subject_token=subject_token,
 706            subject_token_type=subject_token_type,
 707            actor_token=actor_token,
 708            scopes=scopes,
 709            audience=audience,
 710            resource=resource,
 711        )
 712        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 713        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 714        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 715        return self._handle_exchange_response(response)

 717    async def uma_register_resource(
 718        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource: ResourceSet
 719    ) -> ResourceSet:
 720        """``POST /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — register a resource set
 721        (CONTRACT.md §20.1).

 723        The returned ``id`` **is** the AXIAM resource id, directly usable as
 724        the ``resource_id`` of a later :meth:`uma_request_ticket`.

 731        )

 733        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource registration failed")
 734        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

 737        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — read a resource set (§20.1)."""

 747    async def uma_update_resource(
 748        self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str, resource: ResourceSet
 749    ) -> ResourceSet:
 750        """``PUT /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — replace a resource set (§20.1).
 751
 752        **The scope list is replaced, not merged** (§20.2 rule 8). Whatever
 753        ``resource.resource_scopes`` holds becomes the complete declared set;
 754        omitting a scope removes it, which is how a resource server drops an
 755        authority. This method performs no read-before-write.
 756        """
 757        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 758            "PUT",
 759            self._uma_protection_url(f"/uma2/rreg/resource_set/{resource_id}"),
 760            json=self._uma_resource_payload(resource),
 761            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
 762        )
 763        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 764        wire = self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma resource update failed")
 765        return self._resource_set_from_wire(wire)

 767    async def uma_delete_resource(self, pat: SecretStr | str, resource_id: str) -> None:
 768        """``DELETE /uma2/rreg/resource_set/{id}`` — deregister (§20.1)."""

 777    async def uma_list_resources(self, pat: SecretStr | str) -> list[str]:
 778        """``GET /uma2/rreg/resource_set`` — list the ids **this client**
 779        registered (§20.1).
 780
 781        Not the tenant's whole resource tree: a protection scope does not
 782        entitle a caller to enumerate it.
 783        """
 784        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 785            "GET",

 793    async def uma_request_ticket(
 794        self, pat: SecretStr | str, permissions: Sequence[RequestedPermission]
 795    ) -> SecretStr:
 796        """``POST /uma2/perm`` — mint a permission ticket (§20.1).
 797
 798        Scope names are validated **here**, against each resource's declared
 799        set. Asking for an undeclared scope is a ``400``, not a denial — the
 800        two are different failures, and this SDK surfaces the distinction the
 801        server draws rather than flattening it.
 802        """
 803        body = [
 804            {"resource_id": p.resource_id, "resource_scopes": list(p.resource_scopes)}
 805            for p in permissions
 806        ]
 807        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
 808            "POST",
 809            self._uma_protection_url("/uma2/perm"),
 810            json=body,
 811            headers=self._uma_protection_headers(pat),
 812        )
 813        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 814        wire = cast(
 815            "dict[str, str]",
 816            self._handle_uma_protection_response(response, "uma ticket request failed"),
 817        )
 818        return SecretStr(wire["ticket"])
 819
 820    async def uma_exchange_ticket(
 821        self,
 822        *,
 823        ticket: SecretStr | str,
 824        claim_token: SecretStr | str,
 825        tenant_id: str | None = None,
 826        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
 827    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
 828        """Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.uma_exchange_ticket`.
 829
 830        ``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a
 831        ticket for an RPT.
 832
 833        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
 834        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
 835        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
 836        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
 837        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second
 838        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
 839        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On
 840        failure, request a **new** ticket.
 841
 842        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
 843
 844        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
 845          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
 846          resource server instead of for the user.
 847        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
 848          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
 849          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
 850        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
 851          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
 852          that user.
 853
 854        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
 855        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
 856        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
 857        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
 858
 859        Raises:
 860            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
 861                with no wire call.
 862        """
 863        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
 864        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
 865        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
 866        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 867        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 868        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)
 869
 870    async def logout_url(
 871        self,
 872        *,
 873        id_token: SecretStr | str,

 923        url = self._endpoint_url_for_introspect(config, tenant_id)
 924        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
 925        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
 926        return self._handle_introspect_response(response)

 975        §12.1) — step 2 of upstream SSO: consumes the single-use ``state``,

 985    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 986    # §24 WebAuthn / passkeys — the relying-party layer (async twins)
 987    #
 988    # Python has no authenticator, so §24.6b's linked-API helper is
 989    # deliberately absent: §24.6b rule 2 forbids emulating one in software,
 990    # and a "credential" held in process memory is not a second factor. What
 991    # is here is the half that talks to AXIAM, plus §24.6a's JSON bridge —
 992    # which is what lets a Python service be the relying party for a ceremony
 993    # a handset ran.
 994    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
 995
 996    async def webauthn_register_start(self) -> WebauthnChallenge:
 997        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
 998
 999        Requires a session — enrolling a passkey is something a signed-in user
1000        does to their own account — and refuses **client-side with no wire
1001        call** when there is none.
1002
1003        A ``503`` means the tenant's attestation policy requires attestation
1004        and the FIDO metadata service has no usable snapshot. That is a server
1005        configuration state, not a transient failure, so §24.4 rule 2
1006        deliberately does **not** retry it.
1007        """
1008        self._ensure_open()
1009        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_start")
1010        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._WA_REGISTER_START, json={})
1011        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1012        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_register_start")
1013
1014    async def webauthn_register_finish(
1015        self,
1016        *,
1017        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1018        credential_name: str,
1019        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1020    ) -> WebauthnCredential:
1021        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/register/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1022
1023        ``response`` is either the parsed authenticator answer or the
1024        platform's own JSON string (§24.6a rule 2) — Android's
1025        ``registrationResponseJson``, a browser's ``credential.toJSON()``. It
1026        reaches the server unchanged either way: it is the input to a
1027        signature check over bytes this SDK did not produce.
1028        """
1029        self._ensure_open()
1030        self._require_webauthn_session("webauthn_register_finish")
1031        body = self._webauthn_register_finish_body(state_token, credential_name, response)
1032        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1033            "POST", self._WA_REGISTER_FINISH, json=body
1034        )
1035        return self._webauthn_credential(await self._session._send_async(request))
1036
1037    async def webauthn_authenticate_start(
1038        self, *, challenge_token: SecretStr | str
1039    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1040        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1041
1042        The **second-factor** ceremony: it continues a ``login()`` that
1043        answered ``mfa_required`` with ``"webauthn"`` among its methods, and
1044        ``challenge_token`` is that result's ``mfa_token``.
1045
1046        A different flow from :meth:`webauthn_discoverable_start`, not the same
1047        one with an optional argument — see §24.2 for why they cannot be
1048        merged.
1049        """
1050        self._ensure_open()
1051        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1052            "POST", self._WA_AUTH_START, json={"challenge_token": _expose_token(challenge_token)}
1053        )
1054        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1055        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_authenticate_start")
1056
1057    async def webauthn_authenticate_finish(
1058        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1059    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1060        """``POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/authenticate/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1061
1062        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3 rule 1). That is not §14.3's
1063        "MAY adopt" posture: ``device_login`` mints tokens a caller may want to
1064        route elsewhere, and this is the SDK's own primary authentication —
1065        returning a token set without adopting it would make a passkey sign-in
1066        the one way to log in that does not log you in.
1067        """
1068        return await self._webauthn_finish_async(
1069            self._WA_AUTH_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_authenticate_finish"
1070        )
1071
1072    async def webauthn_discoverable_start(
1073        self, *, workspace: WebauthnWorkspace | None = None
1074    ) -> WebauthnChallenge:
1075        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/start`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1076
1077        The **primary-factor** ceremony: nothing precedes it, the server sends
1078        an empty ``allowCredentials``, and the assertion itself identifies the
1079        user. The workspace still has to be named — a discoverable credential
1080        is resolved inside one tenant — but it comes from this client's own
1081        configuration unless overridden, and slugs are accepted.
1082        """
1083        self._ensure_open()
1084        body = self._webauthn_discoverable_body(workspace)
1085        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1086            "POST", self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_START, json=body
1087        )
1088        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1089        return self._webauthn_challenge(response, "webauthn_discoverable_start")
1090
1091    async def webauthn_discoverable_finish(
1092        self, *, state_token: SecretStr | str, response: dict[str, Any] | str
1093    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1094        """``POST .../authenticate/discoverable/finish`` (CONTRACT.md §24.1).
1095
1096        Leaves this client authenticated (§24.3). Unlike its username-bound
1097        twin, this fires the server's ``login.post_auth`` reactor hook (§22.5):
1098        there was no password step for the event to have been fired at.
1099        """
1100        return await self._webauthn_finish_async(
1101            self._WA_DISCOVERABLE_FINISH, state_token, response, "webauthn_discoverable_finish"
1102        )
1103
1104    async def _webauthn_finish_async(
1105        self,
1106        path: str,
1107        state_token: SecretStr | str,
1108        response: dict[str, Any] | str,
1109        operation: str,
1110    ) -> WebauthnLoginResult:
1111        """The shared tail of both authentication ceremonies."""
1112        self._ensure_open()
1113        # §17.1 rule 9 / §24.3 rule 4: memo entries are keyed by subject, and
1114        # this call changes the subject.
1115        self._on_credential_change()
1116        body = self._webauthn_finish_body(state_token, response, operation)
1117        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", path, json=body)
1118        http_response = await self._session._send_async(request)
1119        result = self._webauthn_login_result(http_response, operation)
1120        # The server sets the same axiam_access/axiam_refresh/axiam_csrf triple
1121        # here as it does on a password login, so adoption is the same call.
1122        self._absorb_session_cookies()
1123        return result
1124
1125    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
1126    # §25 Account lifecycle and MFA enrolment (async twins)
1127    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

1129    async def mfa_enroll(self) -> MfaEnrollment:
1130        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
1131        voluntary TOTP enrolment for the signed-in user.
1132
1133        Changes nothing about the current session. In particular it does
1134        **not** clear the §17 decision memo: the subject has not changed, and
1135        discarding a warm memo on an unrelated profile action costs a round
1136        trip on every check that follows (§25.2 rule 3).
1137        """
1138        self._ensure_open()
1139        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_MFA_ENROLL, json={})
1140        return self._mfa_enrollment(await self._session._send_async(request), "mfa_enroll")
1141
1142    async def mfa_confirm(self, *, totp_code: str) -> bool:
1143        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — activate the
1144        factor :meth:`mfa_enroll` offered."""
1145        self._ensure_open()
1146        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1147            "POST", self._AC_MFA_CONFIRM, json={"totp_code": totp_code}
1148        )
1149        return self._mfa_confirmed(await self._session._send_async(request))
1150
1151    async def mfa_setup_enroll(self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str) -> MfaEnrollment:
1152        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/enroll`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — start
1153        the enrolment a ``login()`` demanded.
1154
1155        Reached when ``login()`` returns ``mfa_setup_required``: the tenant
1156        requires MFA and this account has none. There is no session yet — the
1157        setup token *is* the credential.
1158        """
1159        self._ensure_open()
1160        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1161            "POST", self._AC_MFA_SETUP_ENROLL, json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token)}
1162        )
1163        return self._mfa_enrollment(await self._session._send_async(request), "mfa_setup_enroll")
1164
1165    async def mfa_setup_confirm(
1166        self, *, setup_token: SecretStr | str, totp_code: str
1167    ) -> LoginResult:
1168        """``POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/setup/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — finish
1169        forced enrolment and, with it, the login that was interrupted.
1170
1171        Adopts credentials exactly as ``login()`` does, because it *is* the
1172        completion of a login (§25.2 rule 2).
1173        """
1174        self._ensure_open()
1175        self._on_credential_change()
1176        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1177            "POST",
1178            self._AC_MFA_SETUP_CONFIRM,
1179            json={"setup_token": _expose_token(setup_token), "totp_code": totp_code},
1180        )
1181        return self._handle_login_response(await self._session._send_async(request))

1183    async def verify_email(self, *, token: SecretStr | str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1184        """``POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1).
1185
1186        Unauthenticated: a user whose address is unverified may have no session
1187        at all. ``tenant_id`` is a **body** field here — this is not an
1188        ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint, so §12.1 rule 2's query-parameter convention
1189        does not reach it.
1190        """

1192        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1193            "POST",
1194            self._AC_VERIFY_EMAIL,
1195            json={"token": _expose_token(token), "tenant_id": tenant_id},
1196        )

1198
1199    async def resend_verification(self, *, email: str, tenant_id: str) -> None:
1200        """``POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the
1201        **unauthenticated** resend, for a caller with no session.
1202
1203        **Returns normally whatever the outcome.** The address may not exist,
1204        may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this
1205        answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an
1206        anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have
1207        accounts (§25.7).
1208
1209        A caller that *is* signed in wants :meth:`resend_own_verification`,
1210        which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it
1211        is the name you already knew.
1212        """
1213        self._ensure_open()
1214        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1215            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_VERIFICATION, json={"email": email, "tenant_id": tenant_id}
1216        )
1217        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "resend_verification")
1218
1219    async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1220        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1221        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1222        and say what happened.
1223
1224        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1225        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1226        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1227        address.
1228
1229        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1230        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1231        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1232
1233        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1234          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1235          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1236          succeeding.
1237        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1238          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1239        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1240
1241        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1242        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1243        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1244        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1245        """
1246        self._ensure_open()
1247        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1248            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1249        )
1250        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "resend_own_verification")
1251
1252    async def request_password_reset(
1253        self,
1254        *,
1255        email: str,
1256        org_slug: str | None = None,
1257        tenant_id: str | None = None,
1258        tenant_slug: str | None = None,
1259    ) -> None:
1260        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — ask for a reset
1261        mail.
1262
1263        **Returns normally whether or not the address exists**, and this SDK
1264        exposes no way to tell the two apart. That is not an omission to
1265        improve on: a client that surfaced a "no such user" state — even one
1266        inferred from timing — would turn the endpoint into the account
1267        enumeration oracle its uniform response exists to prevent (§25.4).
1268        """
1269        self._ensure_open()
1270        body = self._password_reset_body(
1271            email=email, org_slug=org_slug, tenant_id=tenant_id, tenant_slug=tenant_slug
1272        )
1273        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", self._AC_RESET, json=body)
1274        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "request_password_reset")
1275
1276    async def password_reset_context(self, *, token: SecretStr | str) -> PasswordResetContext:
1277        """``GET /api/v1/auth/reset/context`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the OPAQUE
1278        policy for the account a reset token belongs to.

1281        might have §23 enabled: the client has to build a registration record,

1289        )

1291
1292    async def confirm_password_reset(
1293        self,
1294        *,
1295        token: SecretStr | str,
1296        new_password: SecretStr | str,
1297        tenant_id: str,
1298        opaque: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
1299    ) -> None:
1300        """``POST /api/v1/auth/reset/confirm`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1)."""
1301        self._ensure_open()
1302        body = self._password_reset_confirm_body(
1303            token=token, new_password=new_password, tenant_id=tenant_id, opaque=opaque
1304        )
1305        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1306            "POST", self._AC_RESET_CONFIRM, json=body
1307        )
