The AXIAM SDK's dedicated async REST entry point (CONTRACT.md §1-§10, SDK-Q08).

await client.login(...) returns a typed ~axiam_sdk._models.LoginResult with mfa_required (SC#1) — the same contract as the sync ~axiam_sdk.AxiamClient, on its own dedicated async object. Constructing both an AxiamClient and an AsyncAxiamClient against the same base_url/tenant_slug gives each its own independent _Session (cookie jar, CSRF state, refresh guard) — the two classes do NOT share session state with each other, only each shares consistently within its own sync or async call path.

async def aclose(self) -> None: 
104    async def aclose(self) -> None:
105        """Release this client's local resources (D-19, CONTRACT.md §18).
106
107        Idempotent — calling it twice is not an error. Cleanup runs from error
108        paths, and an error path that itself raises hides the original failure.
109
110        **This does not log out.** §18.1 rule 5: shutting down a client releases
111        *local* resources and never reaches the network. The server-side session
112        deliberately outlives the client object, which is what lets a process
113        restart and resume; an ``aclose()`` that logged out would silently end
114        every user's session on each deploy. Call :meth:`logout` first if
115        ending the session is what you want.
116
117        After this returns, any operation on the client raises ``NetworkError``
118        rather than silently reconnecting.
119        """
120        self._closed = True
121        self._decision_memo.clear()
122        await self._session.aclose()

async def login_opaque( self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult: 
140    async def login_opaque(self, username_or_email: str, password: str) -> LoginResult:
141        """OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.
142
143        The async twin of :meth:`AxiamClient.login_opaque`; see that method for
144        the full contract — including what the ``login/start`` response's
145        ``mode`` field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under
146        ``"optional"`` this retries over :meth:`login` and returns that call's
147        outcome, and under ``"required"``, an unrecognised value or no ``mode``
148        at all it raises :class:`AuthError` and retries nothing. Returns the
149        same :class:`LoginResult` as :meth:`login`, including the
150        ``mfa_required`` case.
151
152        The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it:
153        Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a
154        server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in
155        :func:`asyncio.to_thread`.
156        """
157        from ._opaque import OpaqueLoginStart, start_login
158
159        self._ensure_open()
160        self._on_credential_change()
161
162        exchange = start_login(password)
163
164        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
165            "POST",
166            OPAQUE_LOGIN_START_PATH,
167            json=self._opaque_login_start_body(username_or_email, exchange.ke1),
168        )
169        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
170        if response.status_code != httpx.codes.OK:
171            raise self._opaque_start_error(response, "login/start")
172        started = OpaqueLoginStart.from_wire(response.json())
173
174        try:
175            ke3 = self._opaque_finish_login(exchange, started, password)
176        except AuthError:
177            # §23.4 rule 7, decided identically to the sync client — the shared
178            # `allows_password_fallback` is what keeps the two from drifting.
179            if not started.allows_password_fallback:
180                raise
181            return await self.login(username_or_email, password)
182
183        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
184            "POST",
185            OPAQUE_LOGIN_FINISH_PATH,
186            json={"opaque_session": started.opaque_session, "ke3": ke3},
187        )
188        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
189        if response.status_code not in (httpx.codes.OK, httpx.codes.ACCEPTED):
190            raise error_from_http_status(response.status_code, "OPAQUE login/finish failed")
191        return self._handle_login_response(response)

OPAQUE login (CONTRACT.md §23) — the password never leaves this process.

The async twin of AxiamClient.login_opaque(); see that method for the full contract — including what the login/start response's mode field decides after a failed exchange (§23.4 rule 7): under "optional" this retries over login() and returns that call's outcome, and under "required", an unrecognised value or no mode at all it raises AuthError and retries nothing. Returns the same LoginResult as login(), including the mfa_required case.

The key-stretching function runs on the event loop thread and blocks it: Argon2id at 19 MiB by default is tens to hundreds of milliseconds. In a server handling other requests concurrently, wrap the call in asyncio.to_thread().

async def refresh(self) -> None: 
238    async def refresh(self) -> None:
239        """``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`` (CONTRACT.md §1), routed through
240        the shared single-flight guard (§9) so concurrent 401s collapse
241        into exactly one in-flight refresh call. A 401 on the refresh call
242        itself is ``AuthError`` with no retry (§9.3, Pitfall 4)."""
243        self._ensure_open()
244        self._on_credential_change()
245        observed_access = self._session.cookie_value(ACCESS_COOKIE)
246        if not observed_access:
247            raise AuthError("no access token to refresh — call login() first")
248
249        tenant_id, org_id = self._refresh_identifiers(observed_access)
250        # D-15: diagnostic-only, never a token value. Off by default
251        # (NullHandler); integrates with the consuming app's logging config.
252        self._logger.debug("axiam_sdk: token refresh triggered")
253        await self._session.refresh_guard.refresh_if_needed_async(
254            observed_access, lambda: self._do_refresh_async(tenant_id, org_id)
255        )

async def check_access( self, action: str, resource_id: str, scope: str | None = None, *, subject_id: str | None = None) -> AccessResult: 
293    async def check_access(
294        self,
295        action: str,
296        resource_id: str,
297        scope: str | None = None,
298        *,
299        subject_id: str | None = None,
300    ) -> AccessResult:
301        """``POST /api/v1/authz/check`` (CONTRACT.md §1).
302
303        ``subject_id`` (CONTRACT.md §11.2), when supplied, checks the given
304        subject's permissions rather than this client's own — the caller
305        must hold ``authz:check_as`` server-side. This is what the
306        declarative ``require_access`` helper (§11) passes to check the
307        *request's* authenticated user rather than this client's own
308        (often service-account) session.
309        """
310        self._ensure_open()
311        # §17: consult the memo first. Disabled by default, in which case this
312        # is one dict lookup that always misses.
313        key = memo_key(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
314        memoized = self._decision_memo.get(key)
315        if memoized is not None:
316            assert isinstance(memoized, AccessResult)
317            return memoized
318
319        body = self._access_check_body(action, resource_id, scope, subject_id)
320        wire = await self._authz_post_async(CHECK_PATH, body, operation="check_access")
321        result = AccessResult(**wire)
322
323        # Only a decision the server actually returned is memoized: reaching
324        # here means success, so §17.1 rule 7's ban on caching a failure is
325        # structural rather than a check that could be forgotten.
326        self._decision_memo.set(key, result)
327        return result

async def oidc_par( self, *, request: AuthorizationRequest, redirect_uri: str, scope: str | list[str] | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest: 
442    async def oidc_par(
443        self,
444        *,
445        request: AuthorizationRequest,
446        redirect_uri: str,
447        scope: str | list[str] | None = None,
448        tenant_id: str | None = None,
449        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
450    ) -> PushedAuthorizationRequest:
451        """``POST /oauth2/par`` (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization
452        request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect
453        with.
454
455        PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting
456        ``scope``, ``redirect_uri``, ``state`` and the PKCE challenge into a
457        URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM
458        over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque ``request_uri`` in the
459        redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that
460        cannot be edited into meaning something else.
461
462        **Required for a FAPI 2.0 client** — ``profile: "fapi2"`` refuses a
463        registration that does not set ``require_par``, so such a client cannot
464        authorize any other way (§21.1).
465
466        A §12 extension, not a replacement: ``oidc_exchange`` afterwards is
467        unchanged, and takes the ``code_verifier`` carried on the result.
468
469        Not retried on a ``5xx`` or a transport failure — it is a POST that
470        creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only
471        eligibility exactly as ``oidc_exchange`` does. The safe recovery is a
472        fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).
473
474        Raises:
475            AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no
476                ``pushed_authorization_request_endpoint``.
477            OAuthProtocolError: on any ``error`` the server returns.
478        """
479        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
480        form = self._par_form(request=request, redirect_uri=redirect_uri, scope=scope)
481        url = self._par_url(config, tenant_id)
482        http_request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
483        response = await self._session._send_async(http_request)
484        return self._build_pushed_request(response, configuration=config, request=request)

POST /oauth2/par (CONTRACT.md §26.1) — push the authorization request over the back channel and get an opaque handle to redirect with.

PAR moves the authorization request off the browser. Instead of putting scope, redirect_uri, state and the PKCE challenge into a URL the user agent carries, the client POSTs them straight to AXIAM over an authenticated channel and puts an opaque request_uri in the redirect. What travels through the browser is then a random string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

Required for a FAPI 2.0 client — profile: "fapi2" refuses a registration that does not set require_par, so such a client cannot authorize any other way (§21.1).

A §12 extension, not a replacement: oidc_exchange afterwards is unchanged, and takes the code_verifier carried on the result.

Not retried on a 5xx or a transport failure — it is a POST that creates server state, so it falls outside §16.2's read-only eligibility exactly as oidc_exchange does. The safe recovery is a fresh push (§26.2 rule 4).

Raises: AuthError: when the discovery document advertises no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint. OAuthProtocolError: on any error the server returns.

async def oidc_refresh( self, *, refresh_token: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
512    async def oidc_refresh(
513        self,
514        *,
515        refresh_token: SecretStr | str,
516        scope: str | None = None,
517        tenant_id: str | None = None,
518        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
519    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
520        """``POST /oauth2/token`` with ``grant_type=refresh_token``
521        (CONTRACT.md §12.1) — refresh an ``OidcTokenSet``.
522
523        A **distinct operation** from :meth:`refresh`, which drives the
524        cookie/opaque-token session path at ``POST /api/v1/auth/refresh``
525        (§12.1 "``oidc_refresh`` vs ``refresh``") — the two are never
526        merged, aliased, or made to fall back to one another. Concurrent
527        ``oidc_refresh`` calls collapse into exactly one wire call, and the
528        selected caller's wire call additionally runs inside the same §9
529        single-flight guard the cookie-session :meth:`refresh` uses, so an
530        ``oidc_refresh`` and a concurrent cookie-session refresh can never
531        interleave.
532        """
533
534        async def do_refresh() -> OidcTokenSet:
535            """Perform the actual ``refresh_token`` grant call; run inside
536            :meth:`~axiam_sdk.token.refresh_guard.RefreshGuard.run_exclusive_async`
537            by ``under_guard``, and de-duplicated across concurrent callers
538            by the single-flight coalescer below."""
539            config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
540            form = self._refresh_form(refresh_token=refresh_token, scope=scope)
541            url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
542            request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
543            response = await self._session._send_async(request)
544            # No nonce: rule 6 does not apply to a refresh-issued ID token.
545            return self._handle_token_response(response, config, None)
546
547        async def under_guard() -> OidcTokenSet:
548            """Run ``do_refresh`` inside the shared §9 refresh-guard lock,
549            so it can never interleave with a concurrent cookie-session
550            :meth:`refresh` call."""
551            token_set: OidcTokenSet = await self._session.refresh_guard.run_exclusive_async(
552                do_refresh
553            )
554            return token_set
555
556        result: OidcTokenSet = await self._oidc_refresh_single_flight_async.run(under_guard)
557        return result

async def device_login( self, on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]], *, scope: str | None = None, tenant_id: str | None = None, configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None) -> OidcTokenSet: 
632    async def device_login(
633        self,
634        on_user_code: Callable[[DeviceAuthorization], None | Awaitable[None]],
635        *,
636        scope: str | None = None,
637        tenant_id: str | None = None,
638        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
639    ) -> OidcTokenSet:
640        """The composed §14.3 helper: start the grant, hand the caller the
641        user code, poll to completion.
642
643        ``on_user_code`` is invoked — and **awaited when it returns an
644        awaitable** — before the first poll (§14.3 rule 2). A device rendering
645        a QR code may need to await a paint, and polling before that resolves
646        would defeat the rule as surely as not calling back at all.
647
648        Per §14.3 rule 4 (contract 1.7 errata) this SDK **returns** the token
649        set rather than adopting it. Polling follows §14.2 — see the sync
650        twin's docstring for the full rule set.
651        """
652        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
653        authorization = await self.device_authorize(
654            scope=scope, tenant_id=tenant_id, configuration=config
655        )
656
657        # §14.3 rule 2 — before any polling.
658        result = on_user_code(authorization)
659        if isinstance(result, Awaitable):
660            await result
661
662        schedule = PollSchedule(authorization.interval, authorization.expires_in)
663        while True:
664            if not schedule.tick():
665                raise self._device_expired_error()
666            await asyncio.sleep(schedule.interval_seconds)
667            try:
668                return await self.device_poll(
669                    device_code=authorization.device_code,
670                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
671                    configuration=config,
672                )
673            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified by §14.2
674                outcome = self._device_poll_outcome(exc)
675                if outcome in ("pending", "retry"):
676                    continue
677                if outcome == "slow_down":
678                    schedule.slow_down()
679                    continue
680                raise

821        self,
822        *,

825        tenant_id: str | None = None,
826        configuration: OidcConfiguration | None = None,
827    ) -> RequestingPartyToken:
828        """Async twin of :meth:`axiam_sdk.AxiamClient.uma_exchange_ticket`.
829
830        ``POST /oauth2/token`` with the uma-ticket grant (§20.1) — exchange a
831        ticket for an RPT.
832
833        **This method never retries.** It issues exactly one request and is
834        outside the §16 retry policy — not on ``5xx``, not on timeout, not on
835        any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed *before*
836        the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a
837        retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second
838        concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot
839        attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On
840        failure, request a **new** ticket.
841
842        What this method deliberately does *not* do:
843
844        * **No default ``claim_token``** (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting
845          it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the
846          resource server instead of for the user.
847        * **No auto-narrowing on ``access_denied``** (rule 3). A partial grant
848          is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the
849          application's judgement, not this SDK's.
850        * **No adoption** (rule 4). The RPT is the *requesting party's* token.
851          Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as
852          that user.
853
854        The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client
855        — all answer ``invalid_grant`` with one message. This SDK does not try
856        to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller
857        cannot probe for live ticket handles.
858
859        Raises:
860            AuthError: when no ``client_secret`` was configured — client-side,
861                with no wire call.
862        """
863        config = configuration or await self.oidc_discover()
864        form = self._uma_ticket_form(ticket=ticket, claim_token=claim_token)
865        url = self._token_endpoint_url(config, tenant_id)
866        request = self._session.async_client.build_request("POST", url, data=form)
867        response = await self._session._send_async(request)
868        return self._handle_rpt_response(response)

This method never retries. It issues exactly one request and is outside the §16 retry policy — not on 5xx, not on timeout, not on any transport failure (§20.2 rule 6). The ticket is consumed before the request is evaluated, so a failed exchange has already spent it: a retry cannot succeed, and under concurrency it is precisely the second concurrent redemption a server whose storage engine this SDK cannot attest may admit twice (ilpanich/axiam#302). On failure, request a new ticket.

What this method deliberately does not do:

  • No default claim_token (rule 2) — it is required. Defaulting it to the resource server's own PAT would mint an RPT for the resource server instead of for the user.
  • No auto-narrowing on access_denied (rule 3). A partial grant is refused whole; whether two-of-three permissions is useful is the application's judgement, not this SDK's.
  • No adoption (rule 4). The RPT is the requesting party's token. Adopting it would re-privilege every later call this client makes as that user.

The four ticket refusals — unknown, expired, already used, wrong client — all answer invalid_grant with one message. This SDK does not try to tell them apart (§20.4): the server collapses them so a caller cannot probe for live ticket handles.

Returns normally whatever the outcome. The address may not exist, may already be verified, or may be over the daily limit, and this answers identically in all of them, because it takes an address from an anonymous caller and anything else is an oracle for which addresses have accounts (§25.7).

A caller that is signed in wants resend_own_verification(), which says which of those happened. Do not reach for this one because it is the name you already knew.

async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None: 
1219    async def resend_own_verification(self) -> None:
1220        """``POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification`` (CONTRACT.md
1221        §25.1, §25.7) — resend the **signed-in caller's own** verification mail,
1222        and say what happened.
1223
1224        Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and
1225        this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a
1226        parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary
1227        address.
1228
1229        Unlike :meth:`resend_verification` this reports the outcome, because the
1230        caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the
1231        outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:
1232
1233        * returns — a token was minted and the mail **enqueued**. Delivery is
1234          asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts
1235          everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this
1236          succeeding.
1237        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.ConflictError` (from ``409``) — already verified,
1238          or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
1239        * :class:`~axiam_sdk.NetworkError` (from ``429``) — the daily limit.
1240
1241        §25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on
1242        either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both
1243        failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation
1244        exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.
1245        """
1246        self._ensure_open()
1247        request = self._session.async_client.build_request(
1248            "POST", self._AC_RESEND_OWN_VERIFICATION, json={}
1249        )
1250        self._expect_no_content(await self._session._send_async(request), "resend_own_verification")

POST /api/v1/users/me/resend-verification (CONTRACT.md §25.1, §25.7) — resend the signed-in caller's own verification mail, and say what happened.

Takes no address. The server reads it off the caller's own record, and this signature deliberately offers no way to name a different one: a parameter here would let an authenticated session mail an arbitrary address.

Unlike resend_verification() this reports the outcome, because the caller is signed in to the account it is asking about and none of the outcomes tells it anything it did not already know:

  • returns — a token was minted and the mail enqueued. Delivery is asynchronous and can still fail at the provider; a queue that accepts everything in front of one that rejects it looks exactly like this succeeding.
  • ~axiam_sdk.ConflictError (from 409) — already verified, or the account is in a state that must not be sent a live token.
  • ~axiam_sdk.NetworkError (from 429) — the daily limit.

§25.7 rule 2 forbids falling back to the unauthenticated endpoint on either of those, and this SDK does not: the fallback would turn both failures back into a normal return and restore the bug this operation exists to fix, with an extra round-trip.

1277        """``GET /api/v1/auth/reset/context`` (CONTRACT.md §25.1) — the OPAQUE

1281        might have §23 enabled: the client has to build a registration record,
1282        and building one needs parameters it cannot know before it has a token

1284        ``opaque_mode: required`` is refused, and refused late (§25.4 rule 1).

1289        )
1290        return self._reset_context(await self._session._send_async(request))

57    on a different one by sending a different ``X-Tenant-ID`` on the next
58    request — no re-login, because it already is a principal of every tenant

Whether the account that just signed in is an organization-level principal — CONTRACT.md §5.2.

Such a principal's record lives in its organization's reserved tenant, so its global grants apply in every tenant of that organization, and it can act on a different one by sending a different X-Tenant-ID on the next request — no re-login, because it already is a principal of every tenant there.

An ordinary tenant principal is a principal of exactly one tenant. Changing the header for one of those produces a 403, so this flag is what an application checks before offering a tenant switch, rather than discovering the answer from a failed request.

False on a completed login against a server older than contract 1.31, and False on the two pending outcomes, where no principal has been established yet.

174@dataclass(frozen=True)
175class UmaChallenger:
176    """A configured ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA`` challenge emitter (§20.3, emit half).
177
178    Hand one to :func:`axiam_sdk.fastapi.require_access` (or Django's
179    ``@require_access``) and a denial stops being a bare 403: the guard mints a
180    fresh permission ticket for the pairs the caller lacked and returns it in
181    the header, so a UMA-aware client knows where to go for authority instead of
182    only being told "no".
183
184    **Opt-in, and deliberately so.** Emitting a challenge means minting a
185    credential — a wire call to the Protection API, and a live ticket, produced
186    on a path the caller did not explicitly request. A guard that did that on
187    every denial by default would turn each unauthorized request into a
188    Protection API call, which is a denial-of-service amplifier pointed at your
189    own authorization server.
190
191    **Failure is not escalation.** If minting fails — the PAT expired, the
192    Protection API is down, the resource declares none of the requested scopes —
193    the denial still surfaces as an ordinary 403 without a challenge. A caller
194    who was going to be refused is refused either way; letting a Protection API
195    outage turn a deny into a 500 would hand the outage a second consequence,
196    and letting it turn into an allow would be a security bug.
197
198    :param realm: The protection realm to name in the header.
199    :param as_uri: The authorization server to send the caller to — normally
200        this deployment's issuer, read from discovery rather than concatenated
201        by hand.
202    :param pat: A Protection API Token: a *client-credentials* token carrying
203        the ``uma_protection`` scope (§20.2 rule 1). A user token cannot stand
204        in — a minted ticket is bound to the ``client_id`` that minted it.
205    :param client: The client whose ``uma_request_ticket`` mints the ticket.
206        Async guards need the async client; sync guards the sync one.
207    """
208
209    realm: str
210    as_uri: str
211    pat: SecretStr | str
212    client: Any

A configured WWW-Authenticate: UMA challenge emitter (§20.3, emit half).

Hand one to axiam_sdk.fastapi.require_access() (or Django's @require_access) and a denial stops being a bare 403: the guard mints a fresh permission ticket for the pairs the caller lacked and returns it in the header, so a UMA-aware client knows where to go for authority instead of only being told "no".

Opt-in, and deliberately so. Emitting a challenge means minting a credential — a wire call to the Protection API, and a live ticket, produced on a path the caller did not explicitly request. A guard that did that on every denial by default would turn each unauthorized request into a Protection API call, which is a denial-of-service amplifier pointed at your own authorization server.

Failure is not escalation. If minting fails — the PAT expired, the Protection API is down, the resource declares none of the requested scopes — the denial still surfaces as an ordinary 403 without a challenge. A caller who was going to be refused is refused either way; letting a Protection API outage turn a deny into a 500 would hand the outage a second consequence, and letting it turn into an allow would be a security bug.

Parameters
  • realm: The protection realm to name in the header.
  • as_uri: The authorization server to send the caller to — normally this deployment's issuer, read from discovery rather than concatenated by hand.
  • pat: A Protection API Token: a client-credentials token carrying the uma_protection scope (§20.2 rule 1). A user token cannot stand in — a minted ticket is bound to the client_id that minted it.
  • client: The client whose uma_request_ticket mints the ticket. Async guards need the async client; sync guards the sync one.

def uma_parse_challenge(header: str) -> UmaChallenge | None: 
130def uma_parse_challenge(header: str) -> UmaChallenge | None:
131    """Parse a ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA …`` header value (CONTRACT.md §20.3).
132
133    **This deliberately does not exchange the ticket.** Parsing a challenge and
134    acting on it are separate decisions: the ``as_uri`` names an authorization
135    server the caller has not necessarily chosen to trust, and auto-exchanging
136    would send the requesting party's ``claim_token`` to whatever host answered
137    the 403. The caller decides.
138
139    Returns ``None`` when the header is not a UMA challenge.
140    """
141    trimmed = header.strip()
142    if not trimmed.startswith("UMA"):
143        return None
144    rest = trimmed[3:]
145    # "UMA" alone is a valid, if useless, challenge; anything else must be
146    # separated by whitespace so `UMAX realm="…"` is not read as UMA.
147    if rest and not rest[0].isspace():
148        return None
149
150    fields: dict[str, str] = {}
151    for part in rest.split(","):
152        key, sep, value = part.partition("=")
153        if not sep:
154            continue
155        fields[key.strip()] = value.strip().strip('"')
156
157    ticket = fields.get("ticket")
158    return UmaChallenge(
159        realm=fields.get("realm"),
160        as_uri=fields.get("as_uri"),
161        ticket=SecretStr(ticket) if ticket is not None else None,
162    )

Parse a WWW-Authenticate: UMA … header value (CONTRACT.md §20.3).

This deliberately does not exchange the ticket. Parsing a challenge and acting on it are separate decisions: the as_uri names an authorization server the caller has not necessarily chosen to trust, and auto-exchanging would send the requesting party's claim_token to whatever host answered the 403. The caller decides.

Returns None when the header is not a UMA challenge.

def uma_challenge_header(realm: str, as_uri: str, ticket: pydantic.types.SecretStr | str) -> str: 
165def uma_challenge_header(realm: str, as_uri: str, ticket: SecretStr | str) -> str:
166    """Format a ``WWW-Authenticate: UMA`` header value (§20.3, emit half).
167
168    The resource-server side: having obtained a ticket from
169    ``uma_request_ticket``, tell the caller where to redeem it.
170    """
171    return f'UMA realm="{realm}", as_uri="{as_uri}", ticket="{_expose_secret(ticket)}"'

35        """Build the exception with ``message`` describing the failure
36        (CONTRACT.md §2 construction rule); the exception's own ``str()``
37        prefixes it with ``"authentication failed: "``.

39        ``reason`` is an optional stable, machine-readable code (CONTRACT.md
40        §12.3 rule 3 / §12.4) — populated by the OIDC ID-token validation
41        checklist with one of the seven contract-fixed reason codes
42        (``invalid_alg``, ``unknown_kid``, ``invalid_signature``,
43        ``invalid_issuer``, ``invalid_audience``, ``token_expired``,
44        ``nonce_mismatch``); ``None`` for every other ``AuthError``. It is a
45        code, never free text, so callers can branch on it without parsing
46        ``message``.
47        """
48        super().__init__(f"authentication failed: {message}")
49        self.message = message
50        self.reason = reason

111class NetworkError(Exception):
112    """Transport-level failure: connection refused, timeout, TLS error, DNS
113    failure, or a server-side 5xx (CONTRACT.md §2).
114
115    ``cause`` is set as ``__cause__`` for standard Python exception chaining
116    (``raise ... from cause`` semantics). It MUST only ever be populated via
117    ``error_from_http_status``/``error_from_grpc_status``, which redact
118    sensitive headers from any wrapped ``httpx.Response`` BEFORE constructing
119    this error (D-08, CR-04 carry-forward) — never construct this class
120    directly from an unredacted response.
121    """
122
123    def __init__(self, message: str, cause: BaseException | None = None) -> None:
124        """Build the exception with ``message`` and an optional already-
125        redacted ``cause`` (CONTRACT.md §2 construction rule); the
126        exception's own ``str()`` prefixes ``message`` with ``"network
127        error: "``. See the class docstring for the redact-before-wrap
128        invariant governing ``cause``."""
129        super().__init__(f"network error: {message}")
130        self.message = message
131        self.__cause__ = cause

53class OAuthProtocolError(AuthError):
54    """An RFC 6749 protocol error returned by an ``/oauth2/*`` endpoint as an
55    ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` body (CONTRACT.md §2 sub-type table, §12.3 rule 3,
56    port-brief-addendum item 17).
57
58    A **sub-type of** :class:`AuthError`, not a fourth peer error type:
59    existing ``except AuthError:`` blocks keep matching it unchanged — that
60    backward compatibility is precisely what makes contract 1.4 "non-breaking,
61    additive". Raised for a ``400`` from ``POST /oauth2/token`` (e.g.
62    ``invalid_grant``) and for a ``401`` from ``POST /oauth2/introspect`` /
63    ``POST /oauth2/revoke`` (client authentication failed) — neither of which
64    may collapse into the generic §2 ``400 -> NetworkError`` / ``401 ->
65    AuthError`` rows.
66
67    ``str(exc)`` is always exactly ``"<error>: <error_description>"``, built
68    from the two ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` wire fields, which are also exposed
69    individually as :attr:`error`/:attr:`error_description`. This
70    deliberately bypasses :class:`AuthError`'s own ``"authentication failed:
71    "`` message-prefixing convention: §12.3 rule 3 fixes this class's message
72    to exactly ``"<error>: <error_description>"``, so ``Exception.__init__``
73    is called directly rather than via ``AuthError.__init__``.
74    """
75
76    def __init__(self, error: str, error_description: str) -> None:
77        """Build the exception from the two ``OAuth2ErrorResponse`` wire
78        fields (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 3); ``error``/``error_description``
79        are exposed as public attributes, and ``str(self)`` is exactly
80        ``"<error>: <error_description>"``."""
81        message = f"{error}: {error_description}"
82        Exception.__init__(self, message)
83        self.message = message
84        self.reason = None
85        self.error = error
86        self.error_description = error_description

58class OidcStateStore(Protocol):
59    """Optional server-side store for in-flight ``oidc_begin`` state
60    (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).
61
62    Implement this to back the login/callback handlers with your own
63    storage (Redis, a database, an encrypted cookie). Two invariants are
64    normative:
65
66    1. **Single-use.** :meth:`consume` MUST return the entry *and delete it
67       atomically*, so a replayed callback cannot reuse a ``state``.
68    2. **Expiry.** An entry older than 10 minutes MUST NOT be returned.
69    """
70
71    def save(self, entry: OidcStateEntry) -> None:
72        """Persist ``entry``, keyed by its ``state``, starting its TTL now."""
73        ...
74
75    def consume(self, state: str) -> OidcStateEntry | None:
76        """Atomically fetch **and remove** the entry for ``state``.
77
78        Returns ``None`` when the state is unknown, already consumed, or
79        expired — three cases a caller MUST treat identically (as a failed
80        login), because distinguishing them leaks whether a ``state`` ever
81        existed.
82        """
83        ...

Implement this to back the login/callback handlers with your own storage (Redis, a database, an encrypted cookie). Two invariants are normative:

  2. Expiry. An entry older than 10 minutes MUST NOT be returned.

1771def _no_init_or_replace_init(self, *args, **kwargs):
1772    cls = type(self)
1773
1774    if cls._is_protocol:
1775        raise TypeError('Protocols cannot be instantiated')
1776
1777    # Already using a custom `__init__`. No need to calculate correct
1778    # `__init__` to call. This can lead to RecursionError. See bpo-45121.
1779    if cls.__init__ is not _no_init_or_replace_init:
1780        return
1781
1782    # Initially, `__init__` of a protocol subclass is set to `_no_init_or_replace_init`.
1783    # The first instantiation of the subclass will call `_no_init_or_replace_init` which
1784    # searches for a proper new `__init__` in the MRO. The new `__init__`
1785    # replaces the subclass' old `__init__` (ie `_no_init_or_replace_init`). Subsequent
1786    # instantiation of the protocol subclass will thus use the new
1787    # `__init__` and no longer call `_no_init_or_replace_init`.
1788    for base in cls.__mro__:
1789        init = base.__dict__.get('__init__', _no_init_or_replace_init)
1790        if init is not _no_init_or_replace_init:
1791            cls.__init__ = init
1792            break
1793    else:
1794        # should not happen
1795        cls.__init__ = object.__init__
1796
1797    cls.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs)

class MemoryOidcStateStore: 
 86class MemoryOidcStateStore:
 87    """In-memory reference implementation of :class:`OidcStateStore`
 88    (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).
 89
 90    Per-instance (never process-global), single-use, 10-minute TTL. Expired
 91    entries are dropped lazily on :meth:`consume` and swept opportunistically
 92    on :meth:`save` — no background thread/timer is held, since a library
 93    must not keep the host process alive (port-brief-addendum item 8).
 94
 95    Suitable for a single-process app and for tests. A multi-instance
 96    deployment needs a shared store (Redis, database) — implement
 97    :class:`OidcStateStore` yourself for that; nothing in the SDK assumes
 98    this class.
 99
100    Thread-safe: guarded by a single ``threading.Lock`` so concurrent sync
101    and async (via ``asyncio``'s default single-threaded event loop, or a
102    thread-pool-offloaded call) callers never corrupt the underlying dict.
103    """
104
105    def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float = OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS) -> None:
106        """Build an empty store.
107
108        Args:
109            ttl_seconds: Entry lifetime in seconds. Defaults to
110                :data:`OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS` (10 minutes) and is
111                **clamped to it**: a shorter TTL is honored (useful in
112                tests), a longer one is reduced, because CONTRACT.md §12.3
113                rule 1 fixes 10 minutes as the maximum.
114        """
115        self._ttl_seconds = min(ttl_seconds, OIDC_STATE_TTL_SECONDS)
116        self._entries: dict[str, tuple[OidcStateEntry, float]] = {}
117        self._lock = threading.Lock()
118
119    @property
120    def size(self) -> int:
121        """Number of unexpired entries currently held (tests/metrics)."""
122        with self._lock:
123            self._sweep_locked()
124            return len(self._entries)
125
126    def save(self, entry: OidcStateEntry) -> None:
127        """Persist ``entry`` under its own ``state``, expiring
128        ``ttl_seconds`` from now."""
129        with self._lock:
130            self._sweep_locked()
131            self._entries[entry.state] = (entry, time.monotonic() + self._ttl_seconds)
132
133    def consume(self, state: str) -> OidcStateEntry | None:
134        """Atomically return and delete the entry for ``state``.
135
136        Deletion happens before the expiry check, so even an expired hit is
137        removed rather than left to accumulate, and a second call can never
138        return the same entry twice.
139        """
140        with self._lock:
141            held = self._entries.pop(state, None)
142            if held is None:
143                return None
144            entry, expires_at = held
145            if expires_at <= time.monotonic():
146                return None
147            return entry
148
149    def _sweep_locked(self) -> None:
150        """Drop every expired entry. Caller MUST already hold ``self._lock``.
151        Lazy housekeeping — no background timer."""
152        now = time.monotonic()
153        expired = [
154            state for state, (_entry, expires_at) in self._entries.items() if expires_at <= now
155        ]
156        for state in expired:
157            del self._entries[state]

In-memory reference implementation of OidcStateStore (CONTRACT.md §12.3 rule 1).

Suitable for a single-process app and for tests. A multi-instance deployment needs a shared store (Redis, database) — implement OidcStateStore yourself for that; nothing in the SDK assumes this class.

def classify_webauthn_error(error: object) -> WebauthnFailure: 
173def classify_webauthn_error(error: object) -> WebauthnFailure:
174    """Map a platform ceremony error to its canonical classification (§24.6b
175    rule 5).
176
177    Accepts anything a caller can get hold of: an exception, an error name
178    relayed from a browser or an Android ``CreateCredentialException``, an
179    ``ASAuthorizationError`` code by name. Everything unrecognized is
180    :attr:`WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN` rather than a raise — a classifier that can
181    fail is one more thing for an error handler to handle.
182    """
183    if isinstance(error, str):
184        name: str | None = error
185    elif isinstance(error, BaseException):
186        name = type(error).__name__
187    else:
188        name = getattr(error, "name", None)
189        if not isinstance(name, str):
190            name = None
191    if name is None:
192        return WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN
193    return _FAILURE_BY_NAME.get(name.strip().lower(), WebauthnFailure.UNKNOWN)

211    ``CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest`` or ``GetPublicKeyCredentialOption``,
212    and the value a browser passes to
213    ``PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()``. It is the inner
214    options object: the ``publicKey`` wrapper belongs to the DOM's
215    ``CredentialCreationOptions`` and the platform JSON APIs do not want it.
216
217    Pure local computation, no I/O. Nothing is defaulted, dropped or reordered
218    on the way through (§24.0).
219    """
220    raw = challenge.challenge if isinstance(challenge, WebauthnChallenge) else challenge
221    return json.dumps(raw.get("publicKey", raw), separators=(",", ":"))

The challenge in the JSON form every platform authenticator API takes (§24.6a rule 1).

This is the string an Android app passes to CreatePublicKeyCredentialRequest or GetPublicKeyCredentialOption, and the value a browser passes to PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON(). It is the inner options object: the publicKey wrapper belongs to the DOM's CredentialCreationOptions and the platform JSON APIs do not want it.

Pure local computation, no I/O. Nothing is defaulted, dropped or reordered on the way through (§24.0).

302    state: str
